A Florida woman who was paid $750,000 by a fund for people sexually abused by Jeffrey Epstein has pleaded guilty to falsifying records she used in her application for the money.

Jennifer Percival, a scholar who has written books on autism, entered the plea in federal court in New York on Monday, the same day that she was charged in the case. A transcript of the proceeding was entered in the court record Wednesday.

During her brief court appearance, Percival didn't speak about Epstein and prosecutors didn’t say whether they had reached a conclusion about whether she was, or wasn’t, one of his victims.

Percival, 46, said she applied in late 2020 to a fund set up by Epstein's estate to compensate his victims after he killed himself while awaiting trial on sex trafficking charges. That fund, however, decided she was ineligible for a payment. Court records didn't say why she was turned down.

Then, in 2024, she applied for a share of a new fund created by JPMorgan Chase, which had agreed to pay $290 million to Epstein victims to settle legal claims that the bank should have cut him off as a customer after he was publicly accused of being a serial sexual abuser of underage girls.

In support of that application, she falsely claimed the Epstein estate fund had found her eligible for compensation and paid her $500,000. She provided a copy of her rejection letter, but altered it to make it look like she had been approved.

“The purpose of these actions was to obtain money, which gave me a sense of validation,” she told a magistrate judge, according to the transcript of Monday's court hearing.

The bank's compensation fund wired her $750,000 in 2024 based on her misstatements, but at some point the FBI began investigating.

When she was confronted by agents in late 2025 with the true and accurate rejection letter from the Epstein fund, she falsely said she had successfully appealed and was found eligible after all, Percival said. Then, she gave her own lawyer at the time altered and fabricated emails that were submitted to a federal prosecutor as part of a request for a deferred prosecution deal.

“I know that my actions were wrongful, and I accept full responsibility,” Percival said.

She brought a check to the plea hearing for the $776,031 she owes in restitution. A sentencing date wasn't immediately set.

Percival is the director of Florida Atlantic University’s Center for Autism and Related Disabilities and lives in Boca Raton.

Messages sent to Percival, her lawyer, the autism center and media contacts for Florida Atlantic University were not immediately returned Wednesday.

Neither court records nor anything said in open court make it explicitly clear why Percival claimed to have been entitled to Epstein settlement money.

Federal sentencing guidelines call for her to spend from three to four years behind bars, according to the plea deal she signed with prosecutors, though a judge does not have to follow that recommendation. She was released from custody after the hearing while she awaits sentencing.

Her defense lawyer is likely to argue at sentencing that she has earned leniency through her life’s work helping people with disabilities. A university website listing described her as an “award-winning researcher in disability studies” and said she “participates on national and regional advisory boards.”

A prosecutor said evidence that would have been introduced at trial would have included Percival’s bank records; search warrant returns for her email account, along with testimony by the administrator of two Epstein settlement funds.

News.title: Climate change made deadly Nepal glacier and rock collapse more likely, according to analysis
News.content:

Human-caused global warming thinned glaciers and thawed mountain permafrost, likely helping to destabilize the Himalayan slope that collapsed last month and unleashed catastrophic flooding across Nepal, according to a report released Thursday.

The report by the World Weather Attribution cautioned that climate change was not the sole cause of the Aug. 26 disaster. A large 2015 Nepal earthquake may have weakened the rock years before the collapse, their analysis found.

“This disaster was not an extreme weather event, but the fingerprints of climate change are still clear to see in long-term changes,” said Ben Clarke, a climate researcher at Imperial College London who worked on the analysis, in a press statement.

More than 1,300 people were killed and over 5,000 remain missing after a massive section of rock and overlying glacier collapsed near Nepal’s border with China. The resulting torrent of water, ice, boulders and sediment swept through communities along the Trishuli River corridor and caused billions of dollars in damage.

Climate scientists said that across the Himalayas rising temperatures are causing glaciers to retreat and thawing permanently frozen ground that helps bind fractured mountain rock together. That means climate change can alter not only weather hazards such as heat and heavy rain, but the stability of the mountains themselves — threatening communities concentrated in narrow river valleys below.

The analysis did not determine whether the collapse would have happened without climate change, caused mainly by the release of greenhouse gases when fuels like oil, gas and coal are burned. However, researchers concluded that warming intensified several processes that made the slope less stable over decades.

Global warming weakens high mountain slopes

The report found that one of the clearest changes directly linked to climate change was the rising elevation of the freezing threshold.

The report found that warming had pushed the altitude at which ground remains consistently frozen upward by roughly 100 meters (328 feet) per decade. This exposes rock at increasingly high elevations to longer periods above freezing, thawing permafrost and causing cracks within the ice, ultimately weakening the rock face under the ice.

Jakob Steiner, a geoscientist at the University of Graz who has worked in the Himalayan region since 2006 but is not an author of Thursday's report, said monitoring instruments around 5,000 meters (16,404 feet) now show that some rock and ground no longer remain frozen throughout the year.

“This means that the ground that was sitting below ice for hundreds and thousands of years is now becoming exposed,” said Steiner.

The report found that glacier retreat was another destabilizing force.

Glaciers in the region have been losing mass for decades at a rate equivalent to more than half a meter (about 1.6 feet) of thinning each year, the report found. The Langtang Lirung glacier, located in the region where the disaster occurred last month, has retreated about half a kilometer (0.3 miles) since the 1990s, exposing rock once covered by ice.

The Himalayan region contains the largest volume of snow and ice outside the polar regions. More than 63,000 glaciers in the area feed at least 10 major Asian river systems and support the food, water, energy and livelihood security of billions of people. However, various studies have found that around 78% of the glacier area, located between 4,500 and 6,000 meters (14,763 to 19,685 feet) above sea level, is highly exposed to warming. United Nations reports have found that between 2000 and 2019, glaciers lost 267 billion tons of ice per year, roughly equivalent to the mass of 46,500 Great Pyramids of Giza.

As glaciers shrink, they can remove pressure that helped support adjoining rock walls, while producing additional meltwater.

The weeks before the Aug. 26 collapse were also unusually warm. July and August 2026 were the warmest such months recorded locally, according to the analysis.

“Other than the potential geological factors like earthquakes that are weakening the bedrock, all these other factors are made worse by human-induced climate change,” said Friederike Otto, climate scientist at Imperial College London and one of the report's authors.

Disaster exposes limits of adaptation

The report said the catastrophe also demonstrates how some climate-related risks in the world’s highest mountains may exceed the protection that early warning systems and other adaptation measures can provide.

Nepal has developed disaster risk reduction plans and warning systems, but researchers said the size and speed of the collapse overwhelmed those defenses. Unlike a flood caused by rainfall, which can sometimes be forecast hours or days ahead, catastrophic slope failures in remote high mountains can occur suddenly and remain extremely difficult to predict.

Otto, the climate scientist, said that the mountain ecosystem and societies are more vulnerable to climate impacts than those living in the plains. “Small changes in temperatures affect the stability of the land itself,” she said.

Better high-altitude monitoring, earth observation and warning systems could reduce some risks, the report said. But researchers warned there are limits to adaptation in Himalayan valleys where settlements, roads, hydropower projects and other infrastructure are concentrated along rivers.

Since glaciers and permafrost respond to temperature changes over decades, some mountain destabilization caused by warming has already been set in motion, said the report.

“The most important thing to minimize the risk in this region is to rapidly stop using fossil fuels that lead to increasing global temperatures," said Otto. “All these drivers that we’ve talked about, permafrost melting, glacial melting, etc., will just become worse. And that means that events like this become more frequent.”

News.title: Manchester United booed after being dumped out of League Cup by Brighton
News.content:
After a humiliating defeat to Grimsby Town in their previous League Cup campaign, Manchester United found a different way to exit the competition this time around. The jeers heard at the full-time whistle after throwing away a two-goal lead pointed to more worrying times a year on from Blundell Park.

For the first time in half a century, United lost a game at Old Trafford having led 2-0, highlighting the defensive problems Michael Carrick needs to solve after turning results around last season.

“What the f---ing hell was that?” shouted the home fans, in a chant that may have been aimed at the referee but equally applied to United players, who led through Shea Lacey and Mason Mount’s early goals.

Brighton cut through Carrick’s defence several times before staging their comeback with goals from Charalampos Kostoulas, Pascal Gross and Maxim De Cuyper. All three goals will have Carrick and his analysts rewatching the footage in horror at how they conceded.

“I totally understand the feelings of the supporters,” said Carrick. “We have to accept it. I totally accept it. It’s on me ultimately: as a team what we look like, how we play and what results you get. I take that. I’ll take the praise, I’ll take the criticism and the upset.”

Erik ten Hag used the domestic cups to taste success while struggling in the Premier League, but one of those opportunities is now lost to Carrick, who must be careful not to spiral from a poor start to the campaign into crisis. Sunday’s trip to Fulham before the international break now feels like a big game for United and Carrick.

News.title: Spurs finally score... but still lose
News.content:
“But that is why we cannot say it does not work for anyone. There are players who play every three days with no issues. They are very robust, their performances do not change too much. There are other players where the risk is bigger and the performances are different. I have to learn who is ready to play games every three days and who needs a rest so their performance level is not affected. I thought I had it quite clear in my mind with some, but with others, it is new, even for them, because they have not played as many games. We are learning.”

Liverpool were knocked out in the fourth round of this competition last season, losing 3-0 at home against Crystal Palace. Joe Gomez returns to the squad for the hosts tonight after an injury early in pre-season but Giovanni Leoni, Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Federico Chiesa remain out.

Tottenham are still without a league win or goal this season. Their 0-0 draw at home against Everton Saturday means they sit just above the relegation zone. Tottenham overcame Charlton in the second round, convincingly winning 5-1 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last month.

“I think we are working well,” Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi said. “We played 30 minutes, 25 minutes very well [against Everton]. In that moment we could score two goals. Then we lost maybe the confidence because we did not score. For sure we have to improve. For sure I have big confidence in my players, they are very good players.

“We have to improve, yes. We can say the coach has responsibility if we do not score, yes, I accept, no problem. We did not win any game so far, yes. We are disappointed, sorry for that. But we have other positive things, like I said we did not [concede goals] in the last two games and the things we have to improve, we start our work. Nothing changed in my project and my idea.”

News.title: England cruise to victory led by ‘absolute freak’ Brook
News.content:
Whatever his returns, there has been an extra focus to Brook’s approach this summer, possibly because he has learnt from a grievous indiscretion in Wellington last winter. While others chase the Indian Premier League, he is totally committed to England, taking his break while that tournament is on and playing every match in all formats for his country.

Brook had come to the crease at the fall of the first wicket and, while it is early days, England appear to have added another arrow to their quiver. They handed a debut to opener Aneurin Donald, with his cap presented in the pre-match huddle by Pietersen, the new “specialist mentor”.

Donald has been selected as an “intent merchant”, charged with going extremely hard from the first over, aping Phil Salt, who is missing with a quad injury. He did what he was asked to do, smearing his first ball for two, then pulling six to leg and hammering four through the offside before the first over was out. Another big shot, off Wellalage, in the second saw him well caught in the deep, but 12 off five had kickstarted the innings.

News.title: Max Dowman-mania could make League Cup hottest ticket in town
News.content:
At this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again. The forward’s age and inexperience means he is still used sparingly in those high-priority competitions. The League Cup, by contrast, may prove to be his domain over the coming months.

Dowman’s double at Portman Road made him just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side. The first was Wayne Rooney, for Everton against Wrexham in 2002.

The two goals underlined why there is so much excitement around Dowman. The first was a demonstration of his prodigious dribbling ability, as he weaved through Ipswich’s defence and buried his shot with the weaker right foot. The second showed his composure: a slotted finish, rolled in with ease.

News.title: UK borrowing costs hit 19-year high as global bond rout intensifies
News.content:
The cost of UK government borrowing hit its highest level since 2007 in a fresh global debt sell-off.

The yield on 10-year gilts, a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money, rose from 5.37pc to a fresh 19-year high of 5.41pc on Tuesday as rising oil prices risk reigniting inflation.

Mortgage experts have warned that residential and buy-to-let mortgage rates are set to climb towards 5pc, as market turmoil threatens to filter through to household finances.

Short-term debt costs have also jumped, with the yield on two-year UK bonds surpassing 4.9pc for the first time in three years.

The bond chaos came as Andy Haldane, a former Bank of England chief economist, warned that Labour risked becoming “just a traditional tax and spend socialist government with better TikTok videos”.

He told LBC that John Healey’s original plan for a “low drama budget” had been “torpedoed” by higher borrowing costs and “events over the last couple of weeks”.

He said: “I think that [the bond market turmoil] will mean some hard choices next month at the Budget.”

“Few hard choices so far, but one is looming on the horizon, how any hole to the budget headroom is made good on. Is that a question of tax rises, or is it a question of taking the knife to public spending.”

Mr Haldane has been advising Labour since Andy Burnham took power.

It comes as the US Federal Reserve and the Bank of England face pressure to raise interest rates this week to combat rising prices.

Anthony Brinkman, a portfolio manager at Principal Asset Management, said: “The recent gilt market movements seem to be intent on showing central banks they are out of time – the market is expecting action.”

Borrowing costs around the world are rising after a 20pc surge in oil prices so far this month.

Brent crude tipped above $109 a barrel this week after Houthi rebels in Yemen, considered a proxy for Iran’s forces, seized control of a key port in the Red Sea, threatening shipping.

The US Federal Reserve is expected to raise interest rates on Wednesday in the face of the inflation threat.

As a result, the yield on 10-year US Treasury bonds has surged above 5pc for the first time since 2007.

News.title: AI could transform global inequalities or ‘widen the gap’, warns Bill Gates
News.content:
“AI could be a great equaliser, or [it could] widen the gap”, says Mr Gates. “This is not a long-range prediction. It’s a present-tense choice”.

“We can harness AI for good. But it won’t happen by accident. After all, the market is an extraordinary engine of innovation, but a terrible guarantor of equal opportunity.

“With AI, the gap could grow even faster … That is what makes this moment so urgent. Things are changing rapidly, and the window to shape who benefits from AI, and how soon, is short”.

The key issue holding back the deployment of AI in the developing world revolves around the availability of local data and, in turn, the ability for the technology to scale in environments very different from where it is currently being created.

An app that is trained on billions of hours of American English, will struggle at first with British English (see your spell check) but is next to useless if your local language is Swahili or Chichewa.

More profoundly, an AI tool that allows a farmer in Hampshire to control his combine harvester remotely, will offer little to a smallholder in South Sudan who works the land by hand and faces a completely different array of pests, weather conditions and costs.

The same is true for health. “A community health worker in Rwanda examining a baby with a fever faces different questions than a clinician in a well-resourced hospital - and the AI supporting her needs to reflect that”, says Mr Gates.

He adds: “Most of the world is invisible to today’s AI models. These AI systems were trained primarily on what exists on the internet – and the internet reflects a deeply unequal world. More than 90 percent of the data used to train early, large language models came from English-language sources. The communities that stand the most to gain from AI are largely absent from the knowledge base these tools are built on. They are not just underserved. They are not in the picture at all”.

The new investment aims to help correct that. Mark Suzman, CEO of the Gates Foundation, says investments are already being made with companies including Microsoft and Google to build databases of a much wider range of languages, for instance.

Africa alone has more than 2,000 languages, and for AI’s to be effective there they have to understand what and how people actually speak - “their dialects, accents, and slang, too”.

The investments, he says, are being made on the condition that the intelligence and knowledge they accumulate are made freely available for others to use.

Languages for AI “are true public goods, almost definitional public goods. They need to be freely available to everybody. Once they’re created, they are public goods that can be uploaded onto any AI,” said Mr Suzman.

News.title: Reynolds refuses four times to rule out tax raid on state pensioners
News.content:
The Business Secretary refused four times to rule out retirees paying tax on the state pension from next year.

Jonathan Reynolds declined to reassure pensioners that they would not pay income tax on the benefit for the first time, saying it was a question for the Chancellor.

The comments on Tuesday raised concern for millions of retired people expecting to see their state pension surpass £13,000 from April, forcing them to pay income tax.

However, pensions minister Torsten Bell later insisted Labour would not put up taxes on people who rely on the state pension.

It is still unclear how this will be implemented given the complexity of separating the tax arrangements of different groups of pensioners.

The rise under the triple lock guarantee would drag many pensioners into paying income tax for the first time because their state income would surpass the personal allowance of £12,570.

Rachel Reeves, the former chancellor, said last year that people solely reliant on the state pension would not have to pay the tax.

However, Mr Reynolds was repeatedly asked on BBC Breakfast whether Labour would honour this commitment after the next increase in the state pension in April. He declined to answer four times.

He said: “I’m sorry, that is for the Chancellor and for a Budget.

“The majority of pensioners in this country don’t just rely on the state pensions. Some do, I accept that, but the majority don’t.

“Sometimes when this is looked at, we’re focusing just on the state pension side of this. You’ve got to consider the full range of income retired people in the UK have.”

However Mr Bell, the pensions minister, walked back from Mr Reynolds comments.

He said: “In line with the commitment made at Budget 2025, pensioners who only just exceed the personal allowance will not have the administrative burden of paying small amounts of tax in this Parliament.

“The Chancellor will set out further details on how that commitment will be delivered at the Budget.”

Former pensions minister Sir Steve Webb said only one in 16 pensioners would benefit from this policy.

He said: “Those on the new state pension can expect to see an increase of nearly £500 per year next April.

“But the sting in the tail is that this will take the standard rate of the new state pension above the tax threshold.”

The comments came after official figures on Tuesday indicated the triple lock will rise by 3.9pc from April.

Under the triple lock, the state pension rises each April in line with inflation, average wages or 2.5pc, whichever is highest.

Total pay, including bonuses, rose by 3.9pc in the three months to July, down from 4.2pc in the three months to June.

Pensioners may yet receive a bigger increase if September’s inflation figure is higher than 3.9pc. That will be revealed next month but a higher figure is thought to be unlikely.

Sports.title: Todd Boehly SELLS his Chelsea stake in £1billion deal & steps down as chairman leaving Blues under control of Clearlake
Sports.content:
Next

TODD Boehly has sold his stake at Chelsea in a £1billion deal as he steps down as chairman.

The Blues’ majority owner, Clearlake Capital, will now take “full control of the Club” after buying out co-owners Boehly and Mark Walters.



The club confirmed the news in a statement on Wednesday evening, adding: “There will be no changes to the day-to-day operations, leadership or strategy at the Club.”

Chelsea will now be in the hands of Behdad Eghbali and his business partner José E Feliciano, increasing their stake to 99.9 per cent.



Boehly, 52, and Walter both flogged their 12.8 per cent share in the club for a small profit with Clearlake previously owning 61.5 per cent.

Meanwhile, Swiss billionaire Wyss has also sold his 12.8 per cent but “will remain an important stakeholder and partner in the ownership group”.

The club statement said: “The progress made over the past four years reflects the shared commitment of Clearlake, Boehly and the wider ownership group and the leadership, staff, coaches and players at Chelsea.

“Clearlake intends to continue building on the strategic course the Club is now on and realising the ambition that the ownership group has developed together.”



Boehly, 52, was the face of Chelsea‘s takeover in 2022, when the consortium bought The Blues for £2.3billion from Roman Abramovich.

He initially worked as interim sporting director but has taken more of a back seat in recent years, with Eghbali doing more of the day-to-day work.

The terms of the initial takeover dictated that consortium members could only sell shares to each other during the first 10 years of their ownership in the club.

Talks began in 2024 regarding Boehly or Eghbali buying each other out, with relations between the pair having grown increasingly strained.

In Wednesday’s statement, the American said: “It has been an honour to serve as Chairman of Chelsea Football Club.



“I would like to thank the many who helped secure a bright future for the Club, including the English Premier League, the coaches and players, the talented leadership and staff at Chelsea, and the legions of dedicated fans.

“I have valued my partnership with Clearlake and the wider ownership group, and the collective decisions and investment we have made to support the immediate and long-term success of the Club.

“I am confident that Chelsea is well positioned for continued success under Clearlake’s leadership.”

Eghbali and Feliciano, co-founders of Clearlake Capital, said: “Todd has been an important partner throughout our ownership of Chelsea, and we thank him for his time and contribution as Chairman.

“He will always be a part of the Chelsea story and family.”



They added their focus will be on “investing” in the club and “delivering long-term success for Chelsea and the Club’s supporters”.

It remains to be seen what Boehly, Walter and Wyss will pocket for their individual shares.

Boehly has still been attending Chelsea matches before stepping down and was at the Emirates last week as his side lost 2-1 at Arsenal.

Boehly owns MLB franchise the Los Angeles Dodgers and also has a stake in WNBA side the Los Angeles Sparks alongside Walter.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Walter, 66, is being investigated by the US attorney’s office over alleged financial misdealing.



In August he flipped the Los Angeles Lakers in a £9.2bn deal – just 10 months after buying the premium NBA franchise from the Buss family.

Sports.title: Man Utd used to have Neville brothers… now it’s the Chuckle Brothers after most diabolical display in living memory

MANCHESTER UNITED used to boast the Neville brothers in their backline – it was more like the Chuckle Brothers during a diabolical display against Brighton.

We really did witness one of the most abysmal defensive performances that you could ever possibly see from any side – never mind Manchester United – in living memory.



Before this collapse, United held an astonishing record at Old Trafford, winning 143 and drawing two of the 145 games in which they held a two-goal lead since the 2013-14 season.

That record was blown to pieces as they finally lost one.



Enter Brighton, who have officially become United’s bogey side after winning at the Theatre of Dreams five seasons running.

For the second successive campaign, the Seagulls knocked United out of a cup competition.

Last year, they left United’s season trophyless, and tonight they severely dented their latest attempt at silverware.

With two losses from their first four Premier League games and a chaotic cup exit under their belt, serious questions are already hanging over manager Michael Carrick.

CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

It makes a mockery of JJ Gabriel demanding to be in the squad.

Obviously, he wasn’t the story in the end, given that Brighton did remarkably well to come from 2-0 down to win 3-2.

They were helped really by one of the most amateurish defensive circuses you could see from a Manchester United defence.

From the glory days of Gary and Phil, having Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven at the back together reminded me of Rotherham’s favourite Paul and Barry.

Sports.title: Sunderland 1 AZ Alkmaar 0: Enzo Le Fee the hero as Black Cats win on return to Europe after 53-YEAR absence
Sports.content:
Next

ENZO LE FEE wrote his name into Wearside folklore as Sunderland returned to European football with a bang.

The Frenchman had a penalty saved four days earlier against Arsenal. But he was the coolest man in the North East as his spot-kick secured this 1-0 Europa League win over AZ Alkmaar from the spot.



It may not have been spectacular. It still meant everything to the Mackems.

William Hughes, Dennis Tueart, Robert Kerr and Micky Horswill have enjoyed the fame of being the only players in the club’s history to score in Europe for over half a century.



Now Le Fee has ensured it will be his name being spoken about by future generations.

Five years ago this week Sunderland had just hosted Accrington Stanley before travelling to Fleetwood Town in League One.

Now they have trips to Portugal, Poland, Belgium and Italy’s legendary San Siro to come.

It has been doom to boom since Swiss-French billionaire Kyril Louis-Dreyfus bought the club in 2021.

Two promotions in three years and a top seven finish on their Premier League return is the stuff of dreams for long-suffering supporters.

Of course, this is not the Black Cats’ first foray into European competition.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Not many fans that saw the famous 1973 FA Cup win over Leeds United are still around.

Even less can say they were there at Roker Park to see their side face Hungarian outfit Vasas SC in the resulting Uefa Cup Winners’ Cup campaign.

A decision by greedy club chiefs to double ticket prices backfired. Fuming Mackems voted with their feet as under 23,000 watched them win their first-ever Euro game on Wearside.

Knocked out by Sporting Lisbon in the next round, it has taken 53 years for Sunderland to get back.

And nobody wanted to miss out this time. There was not a spare seat in the Stadium of Light for the start of this new adventure.



The sky was lit up first red and then white pre-game by spectacular searchlights, not used since 2003 and long forgotten about.

The players entered to deafening noise and a huge flag of a ship down the Roker End declared: ‘New shores to conquer!’

Moments later you could hear a pin drop as Enzo Le Fee passed straight to Kees Smit, who sent Mexx Meerdink clear only for Robin Roefs to come to the rescue.

AZ Alkmaar are no mugs. Dutch Cup holders, undefeated and sitting second in Eredivisie and Europa Conference League quarter finalists last term.

But it is now 12 games on the spin they have failed to beat English opposition as Sunderland responded to that scare in style.



Le Fee nearly made amends as Jari De Busser parried away his shot up the other end while the Frenchman’s drive back across the box was missed by both Trai Hume and Wilson Isidor.

Kevin Danso, a winner of competition with Tottenham in 2025, had De Busser working again before Le Fee’s first-time shot from Isidor’s cutback smashed off the post.

Sunderland’s French winger was on a mission and smashed another into the side-netting as the half ended all-square.



Smit’s shimmy round Nordi Mukiele and shot past the far post had Mackem hearts in mouths again before the hosts swung back.

Isidor wildly lashed high into the stand before De Busser’s legs denied Trai Hume.

Finally, just after the hour, Sunderland had lift-off.

A counter-attack found man of the match Le Fee, he cut inside Wouter Goes and went to pull the trigger before being clipped by Weslley Patati.

Penalty. Unlike Arsenal’s David Raya, De Busser guessed wrong as Le Fee slotted home to spark wild celebrations.



Mukiele lifted the scorer high into the air with glee. He was furious moments later when his run into the box was abruptly ended by Mateo Chavez’s bodycheck with no penalty this time.

It was backs to the wall late on as Regis Le Bris men clung on to what they had.

Dan Ballard and then Reinildo threw their bodies in front of two fierce strikes before Dutch goalie Roefs brilliantly denied Mexx Meerdink.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Nilson Angulo could have ended all of the agony late on but somehow had a shot blocked on the line by Elijah Dijkstra with the goal gaping.

Fortunately, it did not matter. Sunderland are off and running in Europe.

It is the first time in 50 years that United have held a 2-0 lead at Old Trafford and lost the game.



The Red Devils were in dreamland after early goals from Shea Lacey and Mason Mount, before the Seagulls took control and mounted a stunning comeback.

Karl Darlow – 4

Shipped three goals in an dreadful club debut. Hardly evoked confidence as he flapped to Kostoulas’ shot.

After a disaster against City, Dalot’s awful clearance was headed back by Luka Vuskovic in the lead up to 2-2. He hardly stood out before then, which was probably a good thing.

Handed his first minutes since a disappointing showing in the embarrassing 2-0 defeat at Hull, Heaven failed to inspire confidence again and stumbled throughout.

The 20-year-old had a mare. He was also far too casual when he tried to shield a ball out of play only for Matt O’Riley to take advantage of his dallying in the first half.

Leny Yoro – 4

The Frenchman won a first start of the season, but was as shaky as his young centre-back partner before it all resulted in being skinned by Pascal Gross.

Sports.title: Man Utd 2 Brighton 3: United’s epic 42-YEAR record broken after throwing away half-time lead to be dumped out of cup
Sports.content:
Next

A SHOCKING Carabao Cup exit plunged Manchester United into crisis mode — and ramped up pressure on Michael Carrick.

Their old nemesis did a number on them again as Brighton now boast wins at Old Trafford in five successive seasons.



It was the first time since 1984 – 42 years ago – that United lost a home match when leading at half-time.

They had led at the break on 550 occasions in that time – winning 498, drawing 52 and never losing. Until today.



The result also ended a 50-year run of never losing when leading by two goals at Old Trafford.

And since Sir Alex Ferguson headed upstairs 13 years ago, United had won 143 games and drawn two at their home having been ahead by at least two goals. Then bogey team Brighton rocked up.

And this third-round collapse — having led 2-0 after just ten minutes — leaves head coach Michael Carrick now possibly past a point of no return.

Two defeats from four in the Prem, including Sunday’s derby loss to ten-man City, was bad enough before 15-year-old academy superkid JJ Gabriel notified the club he intended to quit.

But this result smacked of complacency. Carrick made eight changes, with Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven starting together for the first time at centre-half.

Touted as United’s future, they may have to be consigned to the past after this farce.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Rookie full debutant Shea Lacey, 19, gave the hosts a dream start after eight minutes as he lashed an unstoppable shot past Jason Steele at his near post.

The roar was loud enough on a night where some season-ticket holders could not give their tickets away.

And Lacey earned another cheer when he patted the crest and kissed it in front of the old Scoreboard End.

He almost got on the end of the rebound that Mason Mount converted two minutes later as the Red Devils made a flying start.



Marcus Rashford danced into the area, only to have his effort parried by Steele, and Mount volleyed the ball into the net before Lacey could connect.

That marked Mount’s first goal since Wolves away in December.

Carrick would have been pleased not just with United’s breakneck start, but the identity of the scorers.

Midfielder Mount had looked in good nick during pre-season and was poised to start the competitive campaign, until a foot injury against Paris Saint-Germain in early August sidelined him again.

It was Noussair Mazraoui’s turn in the Red Devils’ problem position of left-back, yet he required treatment midway through the first half.



Man Utd ratings vs Brighton: Lacey a shining light on dark evening as Heaven and Yoro ripped apart MANCHESTER UNITED suffered a humiliating Carabao Cup exit at Old Trafford as Brighton came from two goals down to reach the last 16. It is the first time in 50 years that United have held a 2-0 lead at Old Trafford and lost the game. The Red Devils were in dreamland after early goals from Shea Lacey and Mason Mount, before the Seagulls took control and mounted a stunning comeback. United have not won a domestic cup match since beating Leicester in the FA Cup in February 2025 and again crashed out at first attempt of the Carabao Cup following last season’s horror show at Grimsby. Michael Carrick is feeling the heat after goals Charalampos Kostoulas, Pascal Gross and Maxim De Cuyper ended one of two potential trophy hopes this season. Here’s how SunSport’s Katherine Walsh rated the United players from Old Trafford, as Brighton picked up a fifth straight victory in M16...

Nineteen-year-old Harry Amass was instructed to warm up, and briefly returned, only to be sent back down the touchline by Carrick’s assistant Steve Holland. Yet Mazraoui soldiered on.

Brighton, with a tiny following sheltering from the drizzle, did not initially seem enthusiastic about salvaging the tie, until they belatedly realised just how gettable United’s defence was.



Goalkeeping debutant Karl Darlow flapped at a corner while the raw centre-halves Yoro, 20, and 19-year-old Heaven were both guilty of dozy moments on their first start together.

Malick Yalcouye was sprung through for a one-on-one and opened up his body, but he skewed his attempt well wide of Darlow’s left-hand upright.

Pascal Gross, scorer of seven goals against United during his first spell with Brighton, skied a presentable shot into the Stretford End in the 41st minute as the visitors upped their dominance.

A goal is always coming against this Carrick team and Darlow inexplicably stayed near his goal-line as a long hopeful ball bounced into the path of Charalampos Kostoulas to bundle in on the stroke of half-time.

Heaven misjudged the flight of Jaouen Hadjam’s hoik but Darlow seemed stuck in cement.



Rashford was in crowd-pleasing form but is still yet to register his first United goal since December 1, 2024.



Just as Carrick was preparing to send on Kobbie Mainoo, Bryan Mbeumo and Joshua Zirkzee, the sloppy hosts played themselves into more trouble and Gross got his customary goal against them.

After United’s back four dilly-dallied from left to right, Benjamin Sesko was on his heels from Dalot’s panicky clearance.

The ball travelled all the way back to onside German ace Gross, who controlled and slotted in on 65 minutes to leave Old Trafford stunned.

Carrick’s bid to introduce seniority with his triple change did not work.

Four minutes after the Seagulls levelled, Heaven and Mazraoui ended up in each other’s positions, Kostoulas ran to the byline and squared for sub Maxim De Cuyper to scoop the ball in for 3-2.



Even as late as the 82nd minute and with Brighton ahead, Heaven overhit a pass for Youri Tielemans inside his own area to widespread groans from the crowd. United fans immediately booed.

They were not aimed at the officials — or Brighton.

Bruno Fernandes soon arrived for the salvage operation and prodded the ball through for Rashford.

He, too, was denied by Steele, who stretched every sinew to deflect the ball with his right boot.

Rashford’s race was run now and he made way for Matheus Cunha in the 80th minute.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Brighton ensured last season would end trophyless for the Red Devils. They have now reduced their chances of silverware this season.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick points the blame for 'unacceptable' Man Utd surrender vs Brighton
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick points the blame for 'unacceptable' Man Utd surrender vs Brighton

Manchester United crashed out of the Carabao Cup after throwing away a two-goal lead at home to Brighton to pile pressure on manager Michael Carrick

View 3 Images Michael Carrick speaks after Man Utd's 3-2 defeat to Brighton at Old Trafford (Image: Sky Sports)

Michael Carrick blasted Manchester United’s surrender as “unacceptable” after they crashed out of the Carabao Cup.

‌



United blew a two-goal lead and the Old Trafford faithful then turned on the players with loud boos at the final whistle.

‌



It leaves Carrick under mounting pressure as it was the first time in 50 years that United have lost a game after going 2-0 up at home in any competition.

‌



United boss Carrick said: “We can't accept that as a group. I take responsibility for it. The performance towards the end of the second half, that's on me.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"We'll all be better. We have to be better. We have a big game on Sunday that we have to prepare for. We're out of this competition and we have to go back to winning football matches.

"It doesn't feel good at the moment. It doesn't feel good. We have to go back to winning football matches. We want to win and want to win quickly. The next game is Sunday. That's all I'm thinking about right now.”

Carrick admitted he could understand the feelings of the supporters as they booed loudly at the final whistle. It was loud and angry and left the United boss under genuine pressure.

‌



View 3 Images Man Utd crashed out of the Carabao Cup at Old Trafford

Carrick added: “"Yeah of course, that's pretty obvious! I totally understand the feelings of the supporters.

“We have to accept it. I totally accept it. It's on me ultimately: as a team what we look like, how we play and what results you get. I take that. I'll take the praise, I'll take the criticism and the upset.

‌



“I totally understand it for the way the game went. We have got to win games."

View 3 Images Carrick has asked for patience regarding the JJ Gabriel situation (Image: Manchester United/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Carrick also pleaded for patience and understanding after United wonderkid JJ Gabriel, 15, told the club he wanted to quit.

Article continues below

Carrick added: “We have to be a little bit careful on that one. He's a 15-year-old boy. It's more about the welfare, the care and the attention of JJ as a child really.

“He's certainly a young man. The situation is what it is, but we have to be careful about the exposure and how much we jump on that."

Sports.title: Saudi Pro League club punished after vile Diogo Jota chants aimed at Ruben Neves
Sports.content:
Saudi Pro League club punished after vile Diogo Jota chants aimed at Ruben Neves

Saudi Pro League side Al-Taawoun have been punished after sickening Diogo Jota chants were aimed at the late Liverpool star's friend and compatriot Ruben Neves

View 2 Images Ruben Neves was targeted (Image: Abdullah Ahmed/Getty Images)

Saudi Pro League side Al-Taawoun have been forced to play their next two home matches behind closed doors after Ruben Neves was taunted over the death of Diogo Jota. Al-Hilal star Neves was a close friend and team-mate of Jota, who died in a car crash in July 2025.

‌



The Liverpool and Portugal star and his brother, Andre Silva, both died following an accident in Spain that sent the footballing world into mourning. Neves was a pallbearer at Jota's funeral and now wears his friend's shirt number for Portugal, and has a tattoo on his calf in Jota's memory.

‌



During Al-Hilal's 6-0 win over Al-Taawoun, the latter's fans repeatedly shouted 'Jota' at Neves. The former Wolves midfielder could be seen sarcastically applauding fans before pointing towards the sky.

‌



After the game, Neves told reporters: "I just hope they don't go to pray later after what they did."

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Al-Taawoun have been fined 100,000 Saudi Riyals (£20,000) for their fans' actions, with supporters not permitted for their next two league matches at home. The sanction comes after the likes of Cristiano Ronaldo spoke out about the issue.

‌



Ronaldo, the face of the league, called for the guilty fans to be handed lifetime bans. The Al-Nassr forward said: "The league must take action and punish this kind of fan behaviour.

"This is no longer football, and there have to be limits. People who behave like this should never be allowed to enter a stadium again."

View 2 Images Neves was good friends with Diogo Jota after playing together at Wolves (Image: Getty Images)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

In a statement, Al-Taawoun said: "Such behaviour is completely unacceptable and does not represent the club, its fans, or the values for which the club is known. Sports competition cannot be a justification for insulting, belittling, or bullying others at the expense of anyone's feelings."

The Saudi Arabian Football Federation (SAFF) and the Saudi Pro League (SPL) had also condemned the supporters' behaviour before issuing the punishment. A joint statement said the incident and conduct of some fans during the match were "inconsistent with the values of Saudi football and the principles of sportsmanship".

‌



The statement added that exploiting personal tragedies "for the purpose of abuse or provocation is unacceptable behaviour that has no place in Saudi football".

Neves has previously spoken about how he still speaks to Jota following his passing. "I still talk to him," he said.

"Few people know this. We have a WhatsApp group with Rute (Jota's widow) and Diogo, and it's still there, and we continue to talk there.

Article continues below

“Whenever something special happens, I have the conversations archived on my WhatsApp so I can continue to send him messages."

Sports.title: Man Utd fans turn on Michael Carrick's side as Brighton defeat piles pressure on boss
Sports.content:
THE mood inside Old Trafford turned as quickly as the score line.

At the final whistle, there was a chorus of boos as the Manchester United faithful turned on the players. And if Michael Carrick was not under pressure before, the United boss is certainly feeling the heat now.

This was unforgivable. A lame, meek surrender as United threw away a two-goal lead with some kamikaze defending and unforgivable play.

Incredibly, this was the first time United had blown a two-goal lead in 146 matches and they find themselves out of another domestic cup competition. Again.

‌



Last season, United went out at the first hurdle in the Carabao Cup and FA Cup (the latter to Brighton) and endured the shortest season in the club’s history.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

It did, however, allow Carrick to turn the club’s fortunes around, guide them back into the Champions League and got the job as a result.

‌



But, after a sloppy start to the Premier League campaign - including the Manchester derby to City on Sunday - and now an early cup exit maybe this is proof they plumped too soon with a club legend.

Passion and history will get you so far but Carrick now looks to be struggling as they were hit by their Brighton curse again. That is five wins out of six trips to Old Trafford for the Seagulls.

And it was a pure gift for Fabian Hurzeler’s never-say-die heroes. What a win. But what a lame surrender and an awful week for United.

After teenage wonderkid JJ Gabriel, 15, told the club he wanted to leave, the script turned around when academy graduate Shea Leacey scored on his first start for the club. What a time to get your first goal with a lovely finish after just eight minutes.

‌



It got even better two minutes later when Mason Mount made it 2-0 and surely not even a sloppy United could blow it from here. Don’t bet on it.

View 3 Images Manchester United have been dumped out of the Carabao Cup by Brighton

They did not put the game to bed and were sloppy in defence, the star-studded bench left them short on the pitch and Brighton refused to give up.

You could see Brighton grow in confidence while United began to drop deeper and leave themselves increasingly vulnerable.

‌



They got their reward in first half injury time. Jaouen Hadjam’s diagonal ball split the United defence, Brighton striker Charalampos Kostoulas then fired low past keeper Karl Darlow and it was game-on.

United just did not do enough to put Brighton away. And Brighton just kept going. Diogo Dalot’s clearance was headed straight back by Luka Vuskovic and the ball fell for Pascal Gross.

Brighton forward Gross sidestepped Lenny Yoro, kept his nerve and then fired low past Darlow to level it up. United made it easy. Yoro was exposed that time but Ayden Heaven was so far out of his depth.

View 3 Images Maxim De Cuyper completed the fantastic Brighton comeback at Old Trafford

‌



Brighton were still not done. Kostoulas broke down the right edge of the box, his pull back fell straight to Maxim De Cuyper and suddenly Brighton were in front.

You could hear the boos and frustration begin to ring round Old Trafford as Brighton had turned the game on its head and United were facing another cup nightmare.

Marcus Rashford went through but was denied by Steele. United threw on the big guns to try and salvage a terrible week. But they did not have enough guile, quality or determination to turn it around. Another early cup exit. Another nightmare for Carrick.

Suddenly United’s trip to Fulham on Sunday looks very big for Carrick. Especially as it comes just before the international break.

‌

Sports.title: Biggest VAR blunders ranked after Man City's derby winner leads to Enzo Maresca swipe
Sports.content:
The VAR fallout rumbles on, as it always does. The Manchester derby is the latest game to be embroiled in controversy that stems from decisions taken at Stockley Park.

Erling Haaland's strike was enough to land Manchester City the three points on Sunday, leaving those associated with Manchester United fuming. Michael Carrick didn't shy away from lamenting the decision in the aftermath of the game.

Pro Ref chief Howard Webb has quickly come out and owned up to the error live on TV, after the organisation itself had issued an apology to United within hours of the final whistle.

Once again the issue of VAR and those using it is front and centre. Since 2019 we've had the system in use, and yet the sceptics seem no closer to being converted. Even some of those in favour initially have veered towards binning it, letting mangers and players live with decisions as we did for decades.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

City boss Enzo Maresca has claimed the reaction to the VAR blunder, which failed to acknowledge that Enzo Fernandez had thrown himself at the ball from an offside position, had been overblown.

"Talking about one episode or one moment after that game when we played for 70- 75 minutes with 10 players, I think it's quite poor," said the Italian.

‌



He too claimed that some decisions go for you, some go against you. Maresca even went as far as to reference another VAR mishap in a Manchester derby in 2023, when he was an assistant to Pep Guardiola. The refereeing body didn't apologise for that one.

View 6 Images VAR awarded the goal after it was initially ruled out for offside (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

Any mistake that lives with someone for three years is clearly noteworthy, but we haven't lacked for errors of that magnitude. So what really is VAR's darkest day? We've had a go at ranking the biggest injustices, but make sure you have a go at putting them in order yourself using our interactive tool.

5. Haaland's derby winner

The latest one that's got us all talking. Haaland's strike on Sunday was initally ruled offside, and it looked it, but once the lines had been drawn it was deemed that Patrick Dorgu had played him onside.

‌



That part is accepted, what isn't accepted is that Fernandez had no bearing on the play. The Argentine midfielder was stood in the middle of the box in an offside position and threw himself to try and head the ball, but missed. Lisandro Martinez was clearly impeded as he attempted to cover Fernandez and Haaland.

VAR claimed that because Fernandez didn't touch the ball, all was cleared. Failing to acknowledge the fact he clearly impacted the play. Gary Neville said that he expected an apology pretty soon, and one duly arrived.

4. Rodri dodges handball

During the 2021/22 title race City went to Goodison Park and scored late on via Phil Foden as they looked to pick up a priceless three points. That was soon in doubt though, when Rodri looked to have handled the ball in his own box.

The Spaniard misjudged the bounce of the ball and, as he went to control it on his chest, looked to have seen the ball strike his arm instead. The home crowd were adamant and, such was the length of the VAR check, it was clearly a tight call.

‌



View 6 Images Rodri escaped any punishment as VAR overlooked this handball shout (Image: Sky Sports)

To the naked eye it looked as if the City talisman had made a rare error, but somehow he and Pep Guardiola escaped. Lampard accused the VAR official Chris Kavanagh of being a “professional who cannot do his job right”. Then referees’ chief Mike Riley would personally apologised to Lampard, for whatever that was worth.

3. Fernandes goal given

The one Maresca just refuses to forget. In 2023 City took the lead at Old Trafford before two goals from United turned the game. Bruno Fernandes' strike levelled the game and came despite Marcus Rashford being offside by several yards.

The United attacker raced after the ball and had in it his path, albeit he didn't touch it, but his presence undoubtedly influenced the City defenders. Fernandes then raced from an onside position to score. The offside flag went up, but the officials then reversed their decision as the hosts went on to land a winner.

‌



View 6 Images Marcus Rashford was clearly offside and chased after the ball, but didn't touch it, with Man Utd profiting as a result (Image: Sky Sports)

"Rashford is offside. Bruno Fernandes is not offside. The question is intervening or not intervening in the action," said Guardiola. "When one player shoots and [another] player is in front of the keeper and does not touch the ball, it's disallowed all the time."

Webb later claimed: “I think if that exact circumstance happens again you would probably see a different outcome".

2. Onana punch overlooked

In Erik ten Hag's second year at the helm he decided to rid of David de Gea and bring in Andre Onana, a move that would not prove overly successful. On his first outing the warning signs were evident with the Cameroonian.

‌



As United looked to close out three points in their opening fixture against Wolves, who had been more than good value for a point if not more, Onana had a moment of madness and came out to punch clear a cross, but instead caught Sasa Kalajdzic. No contact made with the ball, but contact certainly made with the Wolves player in the dying stages.

View 6 Images Andre Onana collided with Wolves star Sasa Kalajdzic, but dodged any punishment

No penalty though. Then Wolves boss Gary O'Neil said elite referees manager Jon Moss told him he "could not believe" the error. The three officials involved were overlooked the following weekend.

1. Diaz goal ruled out

Liverpool's first defeat of 2023 came at Tottenham on an evening when Luis Diaz thought he'd scored the opening goal of the night, only to quickly see the offside flag raised.

‌



It looked a tight call to the naked eye and so VAR jumped in to confirm the linesman's call. The glaring issue? They thought the call was onside, so when they 'agreed' with the on-field call, they were agreeing it was offside.

The PGMOL called it a "significant human error" and the audio, later released, showed immediate panic and several people not on the same page. Explicits rang out once they realised the gravity of the error and, after the game restarted they couldn't call it back and simply had to live with their mistake.

View 6 Images Luis Diaz's wrongly disallowed goal at Tottenham three years ago remains one of VAR's darkest days (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images)

Then Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp was quizzed on the apology from the PGMOL but replied: "We won't get points for it. We all thought that when VAR came in it would make things easier."

‌



Now it's your turn...rank these in order, with the most egregious error taking top spot...

Sports.title: Premier League panel unanimously agree on Arsenal red card controversy in final verdict
Sports.content:
Premier League panel unanimously agree on Arsenal red card controversy in final verdict

The Premier League Key Match Incidents panel have unanimously agreed on what the outcome of Arsenal defender Gabriel Magalhaes' kick on Emi Martinez should have been

View 2 Images Gabriel Magalhaes kicked Emi Martinez (Image: Sky Sports)

The Premier League Key Match Incidents panel have unanimously backed Chris Kavanagh and his Video Assistant Referee team's decision not to dismiss Gabriel Magalhaes during Arsenal's encounter with Chelsea. The north London side came away 2-1 victors against the Blues earlier this month, but the match was not without its share of controversy.

‌



Arsenal saw Riccardo Calafiori's strike chalked off for offside, while Kai Havertz's leveller was permitted to stand despite a marginal offside call. Both rulings also received unanimous 5:0 backing from the panel.

‌



But Gabriel's challenge on Emi Martinez may have been the most divisive moment of the match. With Chelsea still leading through Morgan Rogers' strike, Martinez attempted to gather a low free kick from Martin Odegaard. Scrambling for the ball, Gabriel caught the Chelsea goalkeeper in the face when he aimed a kick at the ball.

‌



The ball subsequently slipped from the Argentine's grasp, but no punishment was forthcoming despite protests from Reece James and Joao Pedro. Martinez clutched his head and received treatment but was able to continue.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

VAR chose not to send Kavanagh to the monitor to review the situation, and ultimately the KMI panel have decided that was the right call. The panel is made up of three former players or coaches, one representative from the Premier League, and one from Pro Ref (Professional Game Referees).

‌



They also released the following statement: "The panel unanimously supported the referee's call of no red card. Multiple players were on the ground competing and challenging for the loose ball, and the action of Gabriel was not deemed to be an act of violent conduct or serious foul play."

While that group was unanimous in their backing of Kavanagh, the outcome may come as a surprise to Wayne Rooney. Speaking on Match of the Day, Rooney claimed Gabriel was 'extremely lucky' not to receive his marching orders.

View 2 Images The panel did not believe that Gabriel deserved a red card (Image: Ryan Pierse/Getty Images)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"Martinez has got the ball, and he [Gabriel] boots him on the head," Rooney said. "He's got the ball in two hands, way over the top of the ball, and he boots him in the head, so I think he's extremely lucky to stay on the pitch."

Ashley Young, also on the show, concurred. "I'm exactly the same way," Young said.

Article continues below

"When the ball is on the floor, and Martínez has got it in his hands, Gabriel kicks so high. I'm not sure why it's not gone to VAR, and they've looked at it properly, studied it, because he's nowhere near the ball - I think he's got away with one there."

Sports.title: New season, same Man Utd story - Carrick is now firmly feeling the pressure
Sports.content:
This wasn't just a defeat. This wasn't just a collapse. This wasn't just a cup exit. Another Manchester United managerial project is heading in that one, same direction. And even Michael Carrick recognises that.

"We've gone out of the cup and the feeling around the place feels bigger than that," he said. "I'm happy enough to be honest about that. That's how it feels."

It's a story that's been seen before. A dismal Carabao Cup experience at the first hurdle - this time throwing away a 2-0 lead to exit to Brighton - harks back to memories of Ruben Amorim's disappointing defeat at Grimsby last year, which helped signal the beginning of the end.

A cup exit to the Seagulls was also reminiscent of the FA Cup defeat United suffered to Fabian Hurzeler's side at the start of the year. That was the last match before Carrick returned to the club and sparked a mini-revival. Now it seems like United are back to square one again.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the third round of the Carabao Cup match between Manchester United and Brighton.

Even Pascal Gross scoring the equaliser at Old Trafford brought back memories of how he netted twice at United's home in August 2022 to put Erik ten Hag's tenure on the back foot, in the same way Carrick is facing an uphill battle now.

Gross still doing the business four years later is a great testament to the German's longevity at 35 years old - but it's an even more damning reflection of United's lack of progression in that time.

Since that match in 2022, which came 1,502 days ago, Gross has secured European football for Brighton, left the club for Borussia Dortmund, rejoined the Seagulls, got them back into Europe, watched on as United spent £365m on seven new central midfielders - and still he stood tall above the United midfield.

Image: Brighton's Pascal Gross, right, celebrates after scoring his side's second goal

Around £140m of that pot started for United against Brighton in Youri Tielemans, Mason Mount and Andrey Santos, while a further £70m in Carlos Baleba watched on from the stands as his old club beat his new one. What must he be thinking?

Just like against Hull on the opening weekend of the season, United were outfought by Brighton. "They didn't look fit enough," said Jamie Redknapp. "I don't know if a lot of them do enough. I saw too many players not running back or not looking fit enough."

Many can point towards the nine changes Carrick made, with many of United's players coming into the team after weeks on the Premier League bench. But Brighton also made six changes to their regular line-up, including first starts for the club to four summer signings. What was their excuse?

Once again, the lack of investment in the defensive positions during the transfer market was very clear. The warnings about not addressing that position were there - and a big reason for Brighton turning the game on its head was the defensive displays of Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven.

Image: Michael Carrick looks on glumly as his Manchester United side were beaten by Brighton

"The inexperience of the two young centre-backs definitely showed," said Redknapp. "The pair of them were just inept in everything they did. If you look at Luka Vuskovic, who is 18 or 19, at this level he has aggression, winning challenges, recovery runs.

"And you looked at the two who played at United who played like everything was easy, making bad decisions - there was a difference in Brighton's defending when it came to going about their business."

The difference was seen in the second goal, as Vuskovic won a header ahead of Benjamin Sesko and the ball ran straight through the heart of the United defence for Gross to score easily.

Heaven was caught on his heels and failed to come across. "He doesn't anticipate the danger. Sprint, get to the penalty spot. But he's jogging.

"And Yoro, what kind of an effort is that to stop the shot? How easy was that? This isn't a five-a-side competition."

And for the third goal, Yoro was caught jogging back again as Brighton broke to score - not only highlighting Redknapp's defensive concerns about United, but their fitness ones too. "You've got to sprint Leny," he said. "He's jogging. If he sprints, he gets back and makes that block."

But while United are making familiar mistakes, they are still making unwanted history.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael Carrick responds to the Old Trafford boos after Manchester United were knocked out of the Carabao Cup by Brighton.

Not only was this the first time in 50 years that an opposition team has won at Old Trafford having been 2-0 down in the game, but it was the first time United have lost at home after holding a half-time lead in 551 half-time leads.

The time before the defeat to Brighton came in 1984, which pre-dated Sir Alex Ferguson's time at the club. Throw in a joint-worst start to a Premier League season after four games and the pressure is really growing on Carrick.

United's only win so far this season has been a 5-2 win over Ipswich that saw United struggle for the best part of an hour. And while there have been some mitigating factors - worldies at Everton and a contentious Manchester derby winner - there have been too many of those to be one-offs already.

Fulham

Manchester United Sunday 20th September 4:00pm Kick off 4:30pm

It all sets up a massive Super Sunday game this weekend away at winless Fulham, facing their own early woes under Alvaro Arbeloa. What follows is a three-week international break which is prime time for an early managerial change.

A win at Craven Cottage buys Carrick time. Defeat and it will be a long period of questions.

Sports.title: Leicestershire hit with 27-point deduction for breaching pitch regulations
Sports.content:
Leicestershire County Cricket Club have been deducted 27 points and fined £5,000 for breaching pitch regulations in their victory over Glamorgan in August.

In a statement on Wednesday, the club said: "The Club notes the Cricket Discipline Panel's decision, which imposes an eight-point deduction, an additional eight-point deduction suspended until the end of the 2027 season, and a financial penalty of £5000.

"Under ECB Rothesay County Championship Playing Condition 16.2.6, the 19 points earned in the match concerned will also be deducted from Leicestershire CCC's 2026 Rothesay County Championship total.

"Accordingly, the Club will lose 27 points overall.

"Having received the Panel's decision, the Club is reviewing its position and considering all available options. No further statement will be issued at this time."

Sports.title: Horror own goal sees Fleetwood shock Sheff Utd and book Arsenal tie
Sports.content:
Rhys Norrington-Davies' horror own goal sent Fleetwood into the last 16 of the Carabao Cup for the first time as the League Two side stunned Championship Sheffield United 1-0 at Highbury.

Norrington-Davies nodded a Danny Andrew cross into his own net from close range in the 57th minute to earn Fleetwood a bumper home draw against Arsenal.

Matt Lawlor's side, unbeaten now in nine games in all competitions, had another Andrew effort ruled out for offside and twice hit the woodwork in a dominant second-half display.

Tom Cannon did put the ball in the net for Chris Wilder's visitors, who lined up with only four starting survivors from last Friday's 1-0 league defeat by Wolves, but an offside flag was raised before the striker slid the ball into the net.

United had started positively and Ollie Arblaster had a goalbound effort blocked after only 36 seconds.

But Mark Helm forced Blades goalkeeper Cooper into a seventh-minute save before former United star Ched Evans put his follow-up header narrowly wide.

Jay Lynch denied Joe Rothwell as the visitors attacked again but Cooper was the busier, saving from Lewis McCann and Crispin McLean.

Helm's dipping right-foot effort from 18 yards grazed the top netting as Fleetwood finished the first half in the ascendancy, and they deserved their break from Norrington-Davies' own goal.

United finally came to life in the last 10 minutes with Lynch brilliantly denying Sydie Peck and Ben Brereton Diaz while Cannon saw a goalbound strike superbly blocked.

But the equaliser proved elusive as the away fans made their displeasure known at the whistle.

Sports.title: Abraham double helps Villa cruise past Coventry into fourth round
Sports.content:
Tammy Abraham scored twice as Aston Villa won 3-1 at Coventry City to book their place in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup.

Abraham raced through on goal to give Unai Emery's side an early lead, just their second domestic goal of the season, but it was quickly cancelled out by Victor Torp's stunning free-kick into the top right corner.

The lead was restored just before the break through Ross Barkley's glancing header from Ibrahim Mbaye's corner, with the 18-year-old winger impressing throughout on his first start for the club since his £47m move from Paris Saint-Germain this summer.

Abraham, who had offers to leave before Deadline Day but stayed to fight for his place, helped himself to a second with a simple finish from close range as Villa brushed aside their goalscoring woes to tee up a meeting with Bournemouth in the next round.

When is the fourth round of the Carabao Cup? The fourth round of the Carabao Cup will take place in the week commencing October 26.

The fixture marked the first meeting between the two sides since the 3-2 win for Villa in 2001, which relegated the Sky Blues from the Premier League, and now compounds a tough start to the season for Frank Lampard's side.

They have just one win across their opening five games and will now prepare to face Nottingham Forest, live on Saturday Night Football, in search of their first Premier League goal after returning to the top flight.

The key moments from the CBS Arena

7: GOAL! Abraham races onto Hemmings' pass and slots home the opener for Villa.

14: BLOCK! Ruggeri shot is blocked after a well-worked corner almost led to a quick-fire second.

28: GOAL! Torp curls stunning free-kick into top right corner to draw Coventry level.
