Sports.title: Aston Villa heap misery on Frank Lampard's Coventry with 3-1 Carabao Cup victory... it's early days but this season is already looking alarming for the Sky Blues, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE
Sports.content:
Frank Lampard is learning that even when you lead a club to promotion, management can feel a horribly lonely place when it starts to go wrong.

The former England midfielder guided Coventry back to the top flight for the first time in 25 years but just six games into their campaign, it is already looking alarming. Their defending was awful here, particularly from set pieces, and there were some boos in the second half.

‘When you concede simple goals like we did from set pieces, it’s hard to win against Premier League opposition,’ Lampard said. ‘It’s mentally difficult for players. The soft nature of the second and third goals meant it wasn’t easy to come back.’

The Carabao Cup will not determine Coventry’s season. However, they have now lost five of six in all competitions as Aston Villa claimed their first victory in domestic football this term. Two goals from Tammy Abraham – who was given his chance by Lampard at Chelsea – and another from Ross Barkley sent Villa into round five, with Victor Torp’s first-half equaliser a rare bright moment for Lampard’s team.

Villa boss Unai Emery will be encouraged by Ibrahim Mbaye’s exciting performance, which could earn him a starting spot at Tottenham on Saturday. Villa made seven changes to Coventry’s nine, and both conceded far too many chances. However, there was still no place for Alejandro Garnacho, who has played just 31 minutes since joining on loan from Chelsea.

Tammy Abraham scored twice as Aston Villa beat Coventry City 3-1 in the EFL Cup third round

Unai Emery wanted Abraham to leave this summer, but the striker silenced the doubters here

It was another brutal result for Frank Lampard and his side must dramatically and quickly

‘It’s about working and training,’ said Emery. ‘When he has minutes to play, he must try and play well. He is progressing, but we have players in front of him now.’

Emery was not thrilled that Abraham decided to stay at Villa rather than join Ipswich on loan and in the early exchanges, the Villa boss berated his forward twice for failing to follow instructions.

Abraham answered in the best way possible. George Hemmings collected a pass from full debutant Matteo Ruggeri and slipped Abraham through for a calm finish beyond Dan Bentley.

Villa looked in control until Barkley trod on the ball and fouled Caleb Yirenkyi just outside the Villa box. From the free-kick, Torp curled in Coventry’s first home goal of the season.

Last time these clubs met, in 2001, Coventry lost 3-2 at Villa Park and were relegated from the top flight. They have been all the way to League Two and back since then and the equaliser made them believe once more.

Bobby Thomas robbed Tyrone Mings inside the box but instead of shooting, tried to tee up Sidiki Cherif for a debut goal. Then Gustavo Hamer’s dipping effort flew just wide.

Neither side’s defence was remotely convincing and Ibrahim Mbaye was enjoying his first start for Villa. The £50m signing’s shot rebounded into the path of John McGinn who shot wide, before Barkley went close from 25 yards.

Bentley tipped that one wide but from Mbaye’s corner, Barkley was left alone on the edge of the six-yard box to head Emery’s men back in front.

There was still time before the break for Cherif to shoot straight at Marco Bizot when he should have picked out a team-mate. That would be reserve keeper Bizot’s last involvement as he was replaced by Zion Suzuki for the second half.

If Coventry’s marking was bad for the second goal, they surpassed themselves for the third. This time McGinn drilled a low bar that was dummied by Barkley and Hemmings and steered home by Abraham inside the six-yard box. Not one of the Sky Blues players inside the box had attempted a clearance.

Sports.title: Enzo Le Fee's magic lit up the Stadium of Light to inspire Sunderland to an unforgettable 1-0 win over AZ Alkmaar - and the Black Cats showed why they belong in Europe, writes CRAIG HOPE
Sports.content:
He arrived in the Championship but is deserving of the Champions League. For now at least, Enzo Le Fee is the reason Sunderland are playing, and winning, in the Europa League.

Just when this big occasion demanded a big player to conjure a big moment, the little magician from Brittany reached into his bag of tricks, bamboozled AZ Alkmaar’s defenders and cast a spell over a home crowd that will last a lifetime. They will not forget this night.

It was in the 65th minute that Le Fee won and then converted the penalty that meant Sunderland’s first European fixture in 53 years ended in a deserved victory. No player deserved that place in the history books more than him. He had illuminated the Stadium of Light long before his goal, just like he did last season. The 26-year-old, once of Roma, is a special, special player. He, just like the occasion, did not disappoint.

‘You need good players in the right moment,’ said Black Cats boss Regis Le Bris. ‘And Enzo is a great player. He can create, he can score, he can help in defence. Yes, he’s great!’

Sunderland’s stadium took its name from one of European football’s greatest venues, Benfica’s Estadio da Luz. Opened in 1997 with the dream of continental nights like this, as recently as five years ago there was not so much light as the darkness of League One. It was Accrington, not Alkmaar. Morecambe, not Milan.

Enzo Le Fee coolly converted his second-half spot-kick to earn Sunderland a mighty 1-0 win

His penalty earned Sunderland victory over AZ Alkmaar in their first European game since 1974

MATCH FACTS Sunderland (4-2-3-1): Roefs 8; Mukiele 7, Danso 7, Alderete 6 (Ballard 52, 7), Reinildo 6; Xhaka 7, Sadiki 6; Hume 7, Le Fee 9, Fofana 5 (Angulo 67, 6); Isidor 6 (Brobbey 67, 6) Subs: Moore, Ballard, Methalie, Rigg, Meunier, O'Nien, Ahoka, Jones, Tutierov, Proctor Manager: Regis Le Bris 6 Referee: J Pignard (FRA) 7 Man of the Match : Le Fee

But this is not the story of a plucky underdog, dining at a table at which they do not really belong. Sunderland should be playing in Europe. Sunderland should wave their flags and plant them loudly and proudly on foreign soil this autumn. Come spring, Sunderland should still be in this competition. They’re here not by winning a cup - as they last were in 1973 - but by finishing seventh in the world’s strongest league.

This game was not really about the result, either. It was about ‘I was there’, and I want to be here again. Half a century and more is a long time between European nights. The last one came at Roker Park, against Sporting Lisbon, in a competition that no longer exists. There are supporters here who have lived through an entire generation between continental visitors. For others, this was the first taste, sight and smell of something they had only ever watched and imagined happening elsewhere. For the majority, this was not European football coming back to Wearside, it was the arrival of it.

That was certainly the pervading feeling among those on the playing side. Le Bris and captain Granit Xhaka have been singing from the same hymn sheet this week, chorusing the message that this is just the start, not the final destination. It was, however, never going to be an understated opening to this chapter.

The guttural release when the teams emerged, the same raw sound when League One survivor Trai Hume took out Ayoub Oufkir and the giddy shrieks of the barely believable when Le Fee almost scored direct from an early corner all ensured that the action on the pitch satisfied the anticipation in the stands. This was good. Great, even. Sunderland were playing in Europe, and they were playing well.

Defender Kevin Danso, scorer of one League Cup goal in three years at Tottenham, went in search of the Puskas Award with a 25-yard dipper tipped over by Jari De Busser. Le Fee’s shot then tested the base of the post and this stadium’s plastic seating, given the 48,000 who crashed back into theirs in despair. Or maybe that’s the wrong word, because there was nothing despairing about Sunderland’s performance.

But Alkmaar were good, too. That helped. This felt proper. Loaded with academy products, we will no doubt see the likes of midfielder Kees Smit and forward Ro-Zangelo Daal in the Premier League at some point, even if at inflated fees. Maybe Sunderland, of Europe, will be shopping in that market.

To get here, their recruitment has been rather more shrewd. Take Xhaka. Rarely will £17m be better spent on a player north of 30 years old. To the left of him, on the wing, was a team-mate who could represent the future direction, £31m deadline-day signing Malick Fofana. Not that the Belgium international, 21, appears on the same page as his colleagues just yet.

The page-turner, rather, was Le Fee.

The spirited Black Cats proved why they belong back in Europe on an unforgettable night

There was, though, a period around the hour that was something of a European tutorial for the home side. Their energy, understandably, had faded. AZ took charge, teasing and weaving passes and patterns. How would Sunderland respond? Well, give the ball to Le Fee, of course.

And so, in the 64th minute, he weaved a pattern of his own, right through the penalty area. Just as he was about to shoot, he was tripped. Penalty. He missed last weekend against Arsenal. He was not missing this one.

Sports.title: Man United 2-3 Brighton PLAYER RATINGS: Which player endured a 'very difficult night'? Who did himself no favours after falling down the pecking order - and which three stars disappointed with 4/10 displays?
Sports.content:
Manchester United crashed out of the Carabao Cup as boos rang out at Old Trafford on another damaging night for Michael Carrick.

Brighton were 2-0 down and reeling 10 minutes in after goals from Shea Lacey, marking his first start, and Mason Mount.

United had never lost from the previous 145 games when 2-0 up at Old Trafford but there was a nervousness in the air, not least when Charalampos Kostoulas made it 2-1 just before half-time.

Carrick's side never got a grip on this topsy-turvy game thereafter and goals from Pascal Gross and Maxim De Cuyper condemned United to a Carabao Cup exit at the first attempt for the second successive season.

Daily Mail Sport's NATHAN SALT gives his verdict on Carrick's charges as they bow out of the Carabao Cup…

Brighton produced yet another emphatic performance here at Old Trafford in the Carabao Cup

Michael Carrick looked furious on the touchline at the end as Manchester United crashed out

MANCHESTER UNITED (4-2-3-1)

Karl Darlow – 5

Senne Lammens provides a calmness that others can build off but Darlow seemed to do the opposite on his United debut. Was far too indecisive in coming for Jaouen Hadjam’s through ball that Charalampos Kostoulas scored from. Too often seemed to get his positioning wrong but made a crucial stop late on to keep United in the game for a bit longer.

Diogo Dalot – 4

Never quite got to grips with Brighton’s threat down his side and was given a warning when he switched off and didn’t track the run when Malick Yalcouye ran through the lines to be clear on goal, only to shoot wide. His reckless and aimless hooked clearance left United all at sea for Brighton to score their second goal. An experienced player who didn’t use his experience with so much youth surrounding him.

Leny Yoro – 5

Only his second start of season and this wasn’t a ringing endorsement for more. The young Frenchman did make a number of key interceptions in the first half but neither he nor Heaven looks like the vocal leader in the Harry Maguire mould that any good partnership needs. Looked all at sea for Brighton’s third goal. Deserves some credit for the crucial block he made to stop a near-certain goal with 10 minutes to go.

Ayden Heaven – 4

A very difficult night. Was caught in two minds when both he and Darlow hesitated on the stroke of half-time for Brighton to get their first, found himself way too far from Yoro to leave a gaping hole for the second and was not alert to the danger for the third as he missed the key challenge when Noussair Mazraoui had already blown his assignment.

Ayden Heaven endured a difficult night as Brighton came from 2-0 down to win it 3-2

Noussair Mazraoui – 5

Took a nasty whack from Costinha 20 minutes in and required lengthy treatment but carried on. Plays left back for Morocco and was doing OK here before his deficiencies showed and Brighton exposed his lack of pace for the decisive third goal.

Youri Tielemans – 7

Wearing the captain’s armband, Tielemans came out of this as United’s best player, albeit not a high bar to clear. His vision picked out Lacey for the opening goal and he worked hard at the other end when he made a brilliant last-ditch challenge on Kostoulas late in the first half to deny a goal. Showed some pieces of skill that were highlight worthy, but again like Dalot, Carrick needed to see an experienced player do more to stop the bleeding in a game like this.

Andrey Santos – 5

Had played less than 45 minutes since starting away at Hull City having fallen down the pecking order. This was a rare opportunity and while the Brazilian did make some key interceptions, this wasn’t a performance that exactly made a compelling case for regular starts.

Shea Lacey – 6

A magic moment for a special young player. Lacey was making his first career start for United and netted, in typical Lacey fashion for those who watched him in the academy, his first senior goal, a stunner. Produced a brilliant spin move on the touchline to bamboozle Hadjam, who got a booking for dragging him down. Faded slightly but a bright spot on another grim night.

Shea Lacey became the first United teenager in a decade to score on their first start

Mason Mount – 5

Scored the second goal of the game in smart fashion by crashing an effort into the ground and then the roof of the net. But on a night where he had every chance to take control of a game in the No 10 position that is forever locked down by Bruno Fernandes, Mount became a non-factor after the goal. The disappointment on his face when he came off said it all.

Marcus Rashford – 6

Gave Costinha nightmares and his pace is such a valuable weapon to United. But he had the chance to equalise when through one on one. He looked offside but no flag came and it was a wonder save by Steele to deny him. A player of Rashford’s quality has to score that, though. Was a defining moment on the night.

Benjamin Sesko – 4

Did produce some clever touches to bring team-mates into play and was inches away from nicking the ball past an onrushing Steele as Brighton’s back-pass attempt fell short before the hour. But he didn’t manage a single effort on goal in 65 minutes before coming off on a rough night. It doesn’t feel like he or United know how to get the best out of him.

MANAGER: Michael Carrick – 4

Turn that pressure dial up a notch. He demanded more intensity from his players as this one got away from them and by the end he had his stars out there trying to salvage a cup run. It was all in vain and the noise around his position only gets louder from here.

SUBS

Kobbie Mainoo (for Andrey Santos, 65) - 6

Bryan Mbeumo (for Shea Lacey, 65) - 6

Joshua Zirkzee (for Benjamin Sesko) - 5

Bruno Fernandes (for Mason Mount, 73) - 6

Matheus Cunha (for Marcus Rashford, 82)

Matheus Cunha and Bruno Fernandes were unable to rescue the tie as United crashed out

Steele 7; Costinha 5, Struijk 6, Vuskovic 5, Hadjam 6 (Kadioglu 74, 6); Boscagli 6(Ayari 74, 6), Gross 8, Chema 6; O’Riley 7 (Gomez 66, 7), Kostoulas 7 (Routtar 82), Yalcouye 6 (De Cuyper 66, 7)

Booked: Chema, Hadjam, Ayari

Sports.title: Alejandro Garnacho is already playing catch-up at Aston Villa - if his chance does not come at Coventry tonight, the ex-Man United man may wonder when it will, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE
Sports.content:
Alejandro Garnacho is already playing catch-up at Aston Villa - if his chance does not come at Coventry tonight, the ex-Man United man may wonder when it will, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Since joining Aston Villa, Alejandro Garnacho has played only 31 competitive minutes and received a flea in his ear from his manager. As first impressions go, it has been far from ideal.

Garnacho is not the only Villa player to be told off in public by Unai Emery this season for dawdling on the touchline before being introduced as a substitute.

Yet even though we are still in mid-September, it feels like the 22-year-old is already playing catch-up. He was not helped by a facial injury sustained in pre-season which meant Villa did not pick him for the UEFA Super Cup in mind-August.

With Emery expected to rotate his squad for Wednesday's Carabao Cup tie at Coventry, Garnacho will expect to be involved.

Garnacho’s loan will become a £43million transfer next summer if he hits what Chelsea claim are ‘easily achievable’ targets at Villa. All sorted, then? Not quite.

Alejandro Garnacho will be desperate to start his first game against Coventry on Wednesday

Difficulties settling in

Not many attackers join Villa and start playing regularly straightaway. Morgan Rogers managed it and so has Nicolas Jackson, but Emery has worked with Jackson before and when the Villa boss saw Rogers in the Middlesbrough team in January 2024, it was love at first sight.

Rogers joined Villa for about £10m and never looked back. Now he has gone to Chelsea for £117m. Few absorb Emery’s instructions as quickly as he did.

‘It’s a demanding style and very unique system,’ said captain John McGinn. ‘A lot of work in the classroom.

‘It does take time. It’s not just a case of your normal 4-4-2 or your normal 4-2-3-1. It’s the detail but it’s different. It’s like me going to play international football – it’s a different kind of football. You just need to adapt and hopefully over time we start to grow.’

Emery’s decision to stick to who he knows has not worked this season. Of the new signings, only Jackson, goalkeeper Zion Suzuki and midfielder Joao Gomes have earned his trust, with Ibrahim Mbaye, Matteo Ruggeri and Taylor Harwood-Bellis also looking to make their mark along with Garnacho. Johan Manzambi has only just returned from injury and Leon Goretzka is sidelined with a knee problem.

Garnacho has managed just 31 competitive minutes since joining Villa in the summer

The ghost of Harvey Elliott

Villa might not like to hear it, but loans can be complicated. Last September the club brought in Harvey Elliott from Liverpool on an initial loan deal, which would have become a £35m transfer had the midfielder played at least 10 times.

Elliott made nine appearances across the season, with Emery deciding last November that he did not want him. That left Elliott in limbo for the rest of the campaign with Villa paying a significant salary contribution for a player they knew would rarely feature.

While Garnacho is not at that stage yet, the Coventry match feels big for him. As things stand, it is difficult to imagine the Argentine starting at Tottenham in the Premier League on Saturday.

If he is given a chance at Coventry and takes it, however, at least Garnacho will give Emery something to think about. ‘His attitude his positive,’ said Emery. ‘That is very important.

‘Now he needs time, and hard work every day, which is showing in his attitude. He has played a few minutes and it was not enough – first, the minutes he played and second, the things he showed.

‘But progressively I am seeing him better. The most important thing is to be consistent and demanding in his attitude, and then I believe he will gradually really his best performance.’

Garnacho's situation feels fairly similar to that of Harvey Elliott's at the club last year

Competition for places

The problem for Garnacho is that the battle for spots out wide is fierce. George Hemmings has emerged from Villa’s youth ranks and immediately made an impression on Emery, starting every game so far.

Mbaye may be only 18 but he has not moved for £50m to swap the Paris Saint-Germain bench for the Villa one, while McGinn is not going anywhere either.

Alysson has looked impressive when given the chance this term, and scored Villa’s first league goal of the season. When Manzambi is fully fit, he will probably play as a No10, with Buendia moving back to the wing. So when does Garnacho get his chance?

‘We want to see him at the same level he was at in the first part of the season last year at Chelsea, and before that at Manchester United,’ Emery stressed. ‘He has this challenge, and it’s my challenge to help him achieve it.

‘He needed time to adapt to us and to get his fitness, and there is still work to do. But we have signed him for a long time and we will help him feel comfortable with us, feel confident with us and to exploit his qualities in our tactical structure.’

Garnacho’s best years were 2023-25, when he scored 20 goals and had 17 assists for Manchester United. Find that form again, and the permanent move to Villa becomes a formality. First, Garnacho needs consistent playing time. If that opportunity does not come at Coventry on Wednesday, those around Garnacho may start to wonder when it will.

Sports.title: Carabao Cup fourth round draw as Arsenal and Liverpool discover opponents
Sports.content:
Carabao Cup fourth round draw as Arsenal and Liverpool discover opponents

Carabao Cup holders Manchester City could face Brighto in the fourth round after the draw was made with last year's losing finalists Arsenal taking on Fleetwood

View Image Last season's Carabao Cup finalists, Man City and Arsenal, remain in contention (Image: Alfie Cosgrove/News Images/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Manchester City will face Brighton in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup provided they beat Norwich on Thursday night whilst Premier League leaders Arsenal will take on Fleetwood Town.

‌



Liverpool will face Chelsea in one of the ties of the round having downed Tottenham on Tuesday night. 2025 winners Newcastle have landed a tie against Everton. Manchester United will again be absent for this round after their embarrassing loss to Brighton.

‌



The Gunners made light work of Ipswich on Tuesday night and will seek to win the Carabao Cup for the first time since 1993. Mikel Arteta has fallen short in the semi-final and the final in successive years but will aim to take the final step this season.

‌



City meanwhile have made a habit of winning this tournament and last season's success was their fifth triumph in the last nine years.

Sports.title: Man Utd crash out of the Carabao Cup after crumbling vs Brighton - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Manchester United's season went from bad to worse as they gave up a 2-0 lead to lose to Brighton and go crashing out of the Carabao Cup.

Goals inside the opening ten minutes from Shea Lacey and Mason Mount looked to have set the home side on their way to a much needed win, given the difficult start to their campaign.

But Pascal Gross, who scored his eighth goal against the Red Devils, helped the Seagulls record yet another win over the side from Manchester. United hadn't given up a two-goal lead to lose at Old Trafford since the 1970s, but that stat went up in smoke.

Charalampos Kostoulas pulled a goal back in first-half stoppage time before Gross equalised midway through the second-half. Maxim De Cuyper completed the comeback on the 70 minute mark to send shivers around Old Trafford.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Lacey's strike after eight minutes came after he cut in from the right, taking his left-footed shot early, which flew into the near post. The Old Trafford crowd still reeling from that strike were celebrating again within two minutes.

Mount, who himself has found opportunities hard to come by, was able to seize on an error of Brighton's own making as they attempted to play out from the back. The United midfielder struck his volley into the ground, with the bounce seeing it nestle into the Brighton net.

‌



The Seagulls rallied and eventually got their reward in first-half stoppage time. Kostoulas was able to finish from an acute angle to half the deficit. Little did he know it would ignite a historic comeback. Gross' equaliser owed to some poor defending as a headed clearance from the halfway line found the Brighton man unmarked on the edge of the United box before he turned and finished.

View 4 Images Pascal Gross continued his impressive scoring record against Man Utd

De Cuyper's winner came from close range as he converted after a neat comeback before running towards the corner where the travelling supporters were enjoying another day out in Manchester.

Marcus Rashford missed United's best chance to level as he was denied from close range as the Red Devils saw their Carabao Cup hopes ended at the first hurdle once again. Here's five talking points from Old Trafford.

‌



Brighton jinx continues

In recent years few teams have enjoyed greater dominance over United than the Seagulls, who have made beating them an annual event. Brighton headed to Old Trafford having won seven of their last eleven games against the Premier League giants.

That includes a 2-1 win in Manchester in the third round of the FA Cup last season. That run of form also saw Brighton beat United in the first game of the Erik ten Hag era, that another win at Old Trafford, and a 4-0 mauling back in 2022 when the Red Devils were at one of their lowest ebbs.

You may have thought that a two-goal head start would've been enough to see United get the better of Brighton, but no, the Seagulls recorded another impressive win - their eighth in their last 12 against the Red Devils.

Game mismanagement

Throughout the season United have faced criticism for failing to manage games and, worryingly for them, conceding goals. Sunday was one of the rare occasions they didn't concede twice during a game, but that trend returned on Wednesday as Brighton breached the United goal on numerous occasions.

‌



View 4 Images Michael Carrick had no answers as his side lost for the third time this season

Perhaps a greater frustration for Carrick will the apparent inability of his side to manage games, especially when leading. They failed to see out the contest at Everton recently, conceding late. Against the ten-men of Manchester City they also failed to make it count. But the loss to Brighton by far and away topped the lot.

Lacey's moment

The last time Lacey faced Brighton at Old Trafford he was thrown on after an hour, but failed to see the full-time whistle after being shown a red card. The teenager cut a despondent figure when he walked down the tunnel, thinking one of his early opportunities to impress had come and gone.

Eight months after that forgettable moment the teenager, handed his first start of the season, needed just eight minutes to score the first goal of the night. There are high hopes for Lacey, even in an attack that has established quality, and the 19-year-old's first goal of his career could not have come against a better opponent, even if his efforts will be forget on what was a difficult night for those in red.

‌



View 4 Images Shea Lacey's strike was the perfect start for the hosts

No place for JJ

All the talk regarding United over the past 24 hours is shock as they deal with the bombshell news that JJ Gabriel, one of the most highly thought of players to come through the academy for some time, wants out.

The sensation was named Under-18 Premier League player of the year last season, even though he was only 14 when the campaign began, underlining his potential. He was poised to make his debut against Brighton, but instead is looking for a way out of Old Trafford. His name alongside the No 77 was printed on the back of the matchday programme, but his stay in Manchester could be over before its started.

Sesko pressure remains

In the opening weeks of the season there's been constant theories as to why Carrick doesn't seem to fancy Sesko, at least as a starter. The Slovenian grew into his debut season, coming off the bench to score multiple winners, but a bench player he has remained.

‌



Instead players who aren't natural No 9s have been deployed in those positions ahead of Sesko. But when the former RB Leipzig man got the nod on Wednesday night he did little to push his case for more involvement, especially from the start. Being hooked on the hour mark was not a ringing endorsement.

Sports.title: Bradley Wiggins relishing face-off between best sprinters of all-time in London
Sports.content:
Bradley Wiggins relishing face-off between best sprinters of all-time in London

Matt Richardson will take on arch-rival Harrie Lavreysen at the Lee Valley Velodrome

View 2 Images Matt Richardson will take on all-time great Harrie Lavreysen in London

The two greatest sprinters of all time are set to go head-to-head in London this November according to Sir Bradley Wiggins.

‌



Britain’s newest superstar, Matt Richardson, will try to take down all-time great Harrie Lavreysen of the Netherlands at the London 3 Day at the Lee Valley Velodrome.

‌



Richardson won Olympic silver behind Lavreysen in Paris two years ago while representing Australia, but has since made the switch to GB, having been born in this country.

‌



He made an immediate impact after that nationality swap, beating Lavreysen to European gold in both the individual sprint and the keirin in February. Prior to London 3 Day, he will look to end the Dutchman’s reign at the World Championships in Shanghai, with Lavreysen having won seven straight individual sprint world titles since 2019.

Richardson holds the world record in the men’s 200m flying time trial, and for Wiggins, there is no question that their meeting in Stratford is one for all cycling fans. This is London 3 Day’s third year, and it continues to grow - bringing world-class track racing and a brilliant live atmosphere back to London.

View 2 Images Sir Bradley Wiggins is looking forward to the London event

‌



He said: “For me, that is the highlight of London 3 Day. Harrie is the king of sprinting. How many Olympic titles has he won (five)? Plus his world titles. Matt is the up-and-coming guy that we've managed to poach, although he was born here. He's a world-record holder.

“I mean, these two are probably the greatest sprinters of all time in terms of time. So to have them in London, it's one not to be missed, I'm sure.”

Wiggins knows what it is like to try to take down a legend, having done the same when he first broke onto the scene. At 24, he got the better of Australian great Brad McGee in the individual pursuit in Athens to win his first Olympic gold medal.

‌



And while the sport has moved on in the 22 years since, he believes the mindset required to take down a legend remains the same. He said: “For me, it was McGee definitely at the start, because he took the event to another level at the time.

“He was Commonwealth champion, world champion. Since (Chris) Boardman broke the world record in the superman position, McGee slashed that time in half from what everyone was doing in the world.

“The Olympic titles were the ones that always eluded him. He was my biggest rival going into Athens. I was the current world champion, and he was the world champion two years before that, current Commonwealth champion.

‌



“He was really the benchmark for me, and someone I looked up to as well. He was really my adversary at that time as the Australians always were.

“In this case, I think Matt is on the up. The difficulty for Harrie Lavreysen is maintaining the standard he's set. Winning has become the standard, and there is no second place.

“I think the thing that separates them at the moment, which is odd, is that Harrie still has been the one who's continuing to win world titles, continuing to win Olympics. But Matt has that world record. That proves that he is the fastest man in the world now.”

Article continues below

London 3 Day returns to Lee Valley VeloPark from 13-15 November 2026, bringing together the world’s fastest riders, Olympic champions and cycling’s next superstars. Tickets and information: www.london3day.com | Instagram @LND3DAY

Sports.title: E1 Series commits to Africa with LeBron James and Will Smith backing in Angola
Sports.content:
E1 Series commits to Africa with LeBron James and Will Smith backing in Angola

The E1 Series brought its electric powerboat racing to Angola, with team owners LeBron James and Will Smith in attendance – and the championship has committed to a three-year stay in the country

View 3 Images Team Brady, the reigning two-time champions owned by Tom Brady, won in Luanda (Image: Getty Images)

Electric motorsport took a major leap forward into its thrilling future last weekend.

‌



Dubbed the ‘F1 of water,’ the E1 Series has surged into the sporting consciousness thanks to its celebrity-packed ownership group. But the real action unfolds on the water, where fully electric powerboats - bearing closer resemblance to spacecraft - battle for dominance at speeds exceeding 60 mph across some of the world's most stunning locations.

‌



So, why did E1 decide to bring LeBron James, Will Smith and electric global motorsport to Angola? “There are many different answers to that,” E1 CEO Jamie Copas told The Mirror in Luanda. “We're a global championship, it's important to us to go to new locations, it's important to us to tell our stories where we go. We find locations through long conversations with many different people.

‌



Tiger Woods makes first public golf appearance since car crash after taking break for treatment READ MORE :

Bradley Wiggins insists best is yet to come from Team GB's cycling phenom READ MORE :

“Africa is a really important location for us to come to. We raced in Lagos in Nigeria last year, and it was always the intention to find other locations in Africa where we can race, tell our stories, work with like-minded people, and have the same understanding of the foundational stories that we have and the things we're trying to do.

“When we choose our locations, it's not just about country: it's the backdrop and the location so that we can actually put on a spectacle. We need a waterway that’s long enough, wide enough, deep enough, safe enough, calm enough where we can do this. In Luanda, the Yacht Club was the perfect destination for us.

“From there, our conversations with the government, with the ministry and everyone were just so simple. We have 17 containers full of kit that gets moved around the world, and every venue we go to has different infrastructure so we need support, and we feel we’ve been given that in the local market.”

‌



Copas is convinced Africa is vital to E1's expansion, and left the door open to hosting more than one race per season on the continent. Last year, Lagos proved a resounding success, with a packed-out fan zone underlining the significance of making the sport accessible to as wide an audience as possible.

Luanda drew an equally impressive crowd, with fans going wild for LeBron and Smith. Copas also harbours hopes of recruiting an African pilot to join the paddock in the not-too-distant future.

View 3 Images Westbrook Racing owner Will Smith and Team Alula champion LeBron James both attended the race on Sunday

‌



As far as E1 is concerned, Angola and the wider continent could play a pivotal role in shaping the series' future.

“The reason we do what we do is to tell three foundational stories,” Copas continued. “One's about sustainability, the second one is about gender parity, and the third one is about innovation. Racing is the foundation of what we do, and it gives us the platform on which to produce an amazing spectacle and do the sport that we love doing. But actually, the stories are really important, and that’s why we do what we do.

“We're a global championship, and if you actually look at our audience, we have quite a large market from Africa. We're constantly analyzing the data to see where people are watching, how many people are seeing the spectacle that we create, the racing that we've got on, but also those three stories because the more we can talk about sustainability, gender parity and innovation, the more change we can make.

‌



“Africa is at a point of its development that's incredible, and if we can help with those stories, if we can get more people to see what's happening in the destinations that we go to, wherever it is in the world, especially in Africa, why wouldn't we? We want to work together.

View 3 Images Luanda is set to become a staple of the E1 calendar, with the city inking a three-year deal with the series (Image: Getty Images)

“We're not going to change the world tomorrow, we're not here on that sort of mission, but we are trying to change electric mobility because that brings great benefits around the world and that can help here, that can help in Italy, it can help in America, wherever we go to. But we've got a great opportunity here to tap into a very wide audience and tell those stories more and more that will have an effect on everything we do tomorrow, the day after and the day after that.”

Article continues below

E1 has pledged a three-year commitment to Angola, demonstrating a dedication to advancing the series in a nation and region frequently neglected by international sporting events. Copas added: “It's for us to help tell Angola stories, and I think it’s also for Angola to help tell ours. It’s about that collaboration and partnership. I think the more we can be doing to help with sustainability, green energy, the better.

“Hopefully next year it will be even bigger, the following year it will be even bigger and we can continue to tell the stories. Earlier this week, some of the pilots and some of our team visited a mangrove and planted seeds there. It will be great to come back next year and see how that’s grown. The opportunity to come back is something we welcome.”

Sports.title: Man Utd could lose millions on JJ Gabriel as favourites to sign youngster emerge
Sports.content:
Man Utd could lose millions on JJ Gabriel as favourites to sign youngster emerge

JJ Gabriel has reportedly asked to leave Manchester United, with Real Madrid and Barcelona said to be among those interested in the 15-year-old, which could cost United millions in lost transfer fees

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel has asked to leave Manchester United. (Image: (Photo by Manchester United/Manchester United via Getty Images))

Manchester United losing JJ Gabriel could cost the club millions after the 15-year-old's shocking request to rip up the contract. The Red Devils have been left rocked by the decision from the teenager, who was viewed as one of the shining lights of the club's future.

‌



Gabriel has an Irish passport and will be eligible for a move overseas when he turns 16, next month. Due to current rules, English players are restricted from moving abroad until the age of 18, but there are a host of European giants circling for the coveted attackers' signature.

‌



Paris Saint-Germain, Bayern Munich and Spanish giants Real Madrid and Barcelona are reportedly monitoring Gabriel's situation. If the 15-year-old was to leave for an overseas club, United would only be due around £300,000 in compensation, but moves within England could be a lot more with fruitful - with Liverpool forced to pay at least £2.8m to Chelsea for Rio Ngumoha.

‌



Referee backed over Man Utd VAR decision as Premier League release official verdict READ MORE :

According to the Daily Mail, Gabriel and his family have long harboured ambitions of a move to Spain, with Madrid and Barcelona amongst the interested parties.

United were left blindsided when the prodigious talent made his desire to cut ties with the Old Trafford club known.

PSG, Bayern, alongside the Spanish heavyweights, are reportedly keen on securing Gabriel's signature, leaving United facing an uphill battle to fend off rival clubs when he turns 16 on October 9.

‌



Gabriel had been set to feature in the squad for the Carabao Cup clash with Brighton and Hove Albion, following his hat-trick in the UEFA Youth League victory over Sabah, but that prospect now appears remote.

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel has yet to make his senior debut for Manchester United (Image: Getty Images)

Old Trafford insiders remain uncertain about what prompted the 15-year-old's desire to depart the club, though alarm bells first rang when he wiped all United content from his social media accounts last week.

‌



Gabriel has established himself as a regular fixture in Michael Carrick's first-team preparations and was given his debut during pre-season against Atletico Madrid in Sweden.

The 15-year-old was on course to become the fourth youngest Premier League appearance maker had he been introduced against Hull City on the opening day of the campaign.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Article continues below

However, their loss and the nature of that match prevented such an opportunity, while the 5-2 triumph over Ipswich also presented a suitable moment.

United believe they have exhausted every avenue to demonstrate to the youngster that he represents the club's future, but he will not be given the opportunity to become the youngest ever player in Wednesday's Carabao Cup third-round fixture.

Gabriel became the youngest winner of the Jimmy Murphy award for the club's best young player and scored 26 goals in 29 games last season. He has five in three games this term, including two in his first two matches at Premier League 2 level.

Sports.title: Tiger Woods makes first public golf appearance since car crash after taking break for treatment
Sports.content:
Tiger Woods makes first public golf appearance since car crash after taking break for treatment

Tiger Woods has given an update after a clip of him hitting balls was shared

View 2 Images Tiger Woods has returned to the golf course (Image: Getty Images)

Tiger Woods has shared footage of him hitting golf balls for the first time since his car accident and break from the game. The 15-time major champion was seen practising on the range at Liberty National in New Jersey ahead of the upcoming Nexus Cup, an amateur event Woods is hosting to raise funds for his TGR Foundation.

‌



The 50-year-old also held a clinic at which the master of ceremonies asked him about his game. He said: "I can hit pretty much anything."

‌



The PGA Tour also posted a video, which Woods shared, of him hitting a crisp iron shot off a practice tee. The caption reads: "Tiger Woods is back on the range! His last PGA Tour start was July 2024."

‌



While it is unclear whether he was preparing for a comeback, the tone of the PGA Tour's post suggests it isn't out of the question.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Woods escaped unhurt after rolling his Land Rover in March and subsequently took time out of the public eye to "seek treatment and focus on my health." Earlier this month, he pleaded no contest to a charge of reckless driving and accepted a five-year suspension of his driving licence and a £742 fine. He pleaded not guilty to the original DUI charge.

‌



Tiger Woods avoids jail with last-minute plea deal over reckless driving charge that ended in horror crash READ MORE :

LIV Golf files for bankruptcy protection as star players owed £33m free to leave READ MORE :

A no-contest plea is not an admission of guilt, but means the accused will offer no defence. The plea is treated as a conviction in the criminal justice system.

He arrived at the courthouse in County Martin, Florida, with his girlfriend, Vanessa Trump, the former daughter-in-law of President Donald Trump . She sat behind him during the proceedings, which were held in a mostly empty courtroom.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Neither Woods nor the person in the other vehicle was injured in the crash but the star's Land Rover caused £3,700 in damage to the truck, according to a police report.

Woods is considered among the greatest golfers of all time and has won 15 major titles. That includes three Open Championship and US Open titles apiece, four editions of the PGA Championship and The Masters six times.

View 2 Images Woods leaves the courthouse in Florida (Image: Getty Images)

The last of his major championship victories came in 2019 amid huge fanfare at Augusta. He hasn't appeared in a PGA Tour event since the 2024 Open at Royal Troon, where he failed to make the cut.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
