Tech.title: Here’s What Snap’s Expensive Specs Can Actually Do
OpenAI Creates a New Framework to Disclose Bad AI Behavior
Tech.content:
OpenAI announced a new framework on Wednesday for how it publicly discloses AI misalignment incidents, which the company says it hopes will help inform similar standards across the industry. The company is also releasing new information about several examples of AI model misalignment it identified in the past year.

“As models advance and become more widely deployed, decisions about AI development need evidence that people outside the companies building frontier models can examine,” Kai Chen, OpenAI’s newly appointed head of alignment research, tells WIRED. “We don't believe that the AI industry has solved alignment and monitoring to a sufficient degree to continue responsibly scaling at maximum speed.”

In a briefing with WIRED, an OpenAI official said the company previously disclosed misalignment incidents too infrequently. The official, who agreed to the briefing on the condition of anonymity, said the new framework is designed to make it easier for OpenAI to quickly inform the public when it discovers that its AI models are behaving in unexpected ways, even before it can fully investigate, explain, or mitigate the behavior.

The framework outlines methods for OpenAI employees to report misalignment incidents to the company’s senior safety and alignment leaders, who will then determine whether further investigation is needed. OpenAI says it plans to develop more objective disclosure criteria in collaboration with other AI developers, external researchers, industry standards bodies, and regulators. The company says it’s actively working on proposed reporting mechanisms for disclosing safety, security, and misalignment incidents to the US federal government.

“At the moment, there is no industry-wide framework with explicit standards for how AI developers should disclose examples of misalignment in their models,” OpenAI said in a blog post. “We hope that the framework we’re outlining today is a first step toward creating such standards, setting out which misalignment instances developers should disclose and what their reports should contain.”

OpenAI is releasing the framework at a critical juncture for the AI industry. Last weekend, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman signaled support for Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei’s proposal for the tech industry to coordinate on slowing AI development. The call to action came just days after AI researcher Jacob Coxon resigned from Anthropic and subsequently went viral for warning the public that the race among frontier labs to develop increasingly advanced AI was putting humanity’s safety at stake.

The calls for an AI slowdown have been met with resistance by President Trump’s administration, which has argued that the industry does not need new laws or regulations to ensure its technology is safe.

Two of the misalignment examples OpenAI shared on Wednesday involved the company’s internal, unreleased AI models, which OpenAI says uploaded files to the internet despite not being instructed to do so.

One of the incidents happened in October 2025, when OpenAI says it was testing one of its models on its ability to cite publicly available data in its answers. But when the model couldn’t find the information it needed, it uploaded a file to a temporary file hosting service, which it then later tried to cite in its answer. The company says this appeared to be an attempt to exploit an automated grading system used to assess the model’s proficiency on the benchmark.

In another example from April of this year, OpenAI says a group of agents was tasked with completing a “workbook” together using only local files. When the agents struggled to share files with one another, one of the agents uploaded them to the public internet and shared a link with the other agents.

In another incident, which OpenAI says it discovered last month, an unreleased version of its GPT-6 Astra AI model appeared to give itself “jailbreaking-like instructions.” In several scenarios, the model essentially prompted itself to ignore developer instructions, take on a new persona, or limit how long model responses could be. While these jailbreaking-like attempts happened rarely and were effective to varying degrees, OpenAI says the behavior raised concerns internally. In the training run for the version of Astra that was released publicly, the company says it has not observed any instances of the model trying to jailbreak itself.

Tech.title: Washington Won’t Be Regulating AI Anytime Soon
Tech.content:
For weeks, Washington has been abuzz with talk of needing to push through some sort of AI regulation amid mounting concerns about the risks of highly capable frontier AI models going rogue.

But there is no reason to think any one measure can win the support of the White House, where officials have paused work on creating a FINRA-style regulatory body after President Donald Trump soured on the idea, or of Capitol Hill, where lawmakers have competing proposals that lack the votes to pass.

White House aides initially started sketching out a framework for an AI oversight agency connected to the administration soon after Google DeepMind’s cofounder Demis Hassabis floated the idea in a July 14 essay and in briefings to senior officials, according to sources familiar with the matter.

The Treasury Department and the White House’s Office of Science and Technology Policy envisioned a body where leading AI labs would self-regulate the development of frontier models, and they put together a preliminary draft to see what it could look like if executed.

But when a chorus of tech executives—including Trump’s former AI czar David Sacks and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg—learned of the effort, they one by one called Trump in August to express their opposition. The proposal has since been left in limbo.

Since then, there have been no new AI oversight proposals seriously under consideration at the White House, the sources say, not least as Trump has doubled down in recent days of rejecting any overt regulation and called AI safety concerns a “hoax” in a recent Truth Social post.

Tech.title: A Deal Hunter’s Guide to Amazon Prime Big Deal Days (2026)
Tech.content:
Amazon Prime Day events are some of the most confusing shopping occasions in existence: It’s not even a single “day" anymore. Amazon promises “millions of deals”—but the displayed discounts are often misleading, and while it’s advertised as a members-only event, some deals are available to people who don’t subscribe to Prime. Add in the frenzy of limited-time Lightning Deals and you’ve got a perfect recipe for spending too much money on stuff you don't even really want.

Fear not! I've been covering deals for over a decade and am here to help. WIRED’s Reviews team is familiar with common shopping pitfalls, and we closely track the best Prime Big Deal Days prices. What time do sales start and end? How do you tell whether a deal is actually a deal? We pooled our collective expertise to get you prepared for the latest Amazon Prime Day Event, which is technically dubbed “Amazon Prime Big Deal Days” and will be on October 6 and October 7 this year.

When Is Amazon Prime Day?

Amazon Prime Day has a main sale in the summer and a secondary sale—called Prime Big Deal Days—in the fall. This year, Prime Big Deal Days will take place on Tuesday and Wednesday, October 6 and October 7.

When Do Prime Day Deals Start?

The event kicks off at 3:01 am Eastern time (midnight Pacific) and runs for 48 hours. New deals will drop three times each day of the event, at 3 am, 11 am, and 4 pm ET, with Lightning Deals going live sporadically as well. WIRED will cover the best deals from both Amazon and retailers that have competing sales.

Are Prime Day Deals Only for Prime Members?

That's the official line: You need to be an Amazon Prime member to shop Amazon Prime Day deals. There is a free 30-day trial available for eligible new accounts. (Prime membership comes with a lot of perks, and we've rounded up all of them here.) The trial will let you get in on the sale—just remember to cancel your membership to avoid any subsequent $15 monthly renewal charges.

However, there are usually plenty of discounts available if you're not a subscriber. Other major retailers like Best Buy, Target, and Walmart typically hold competing sales during Prime Days. The prices are often close to what Amazon is offering on the same products, and sometimes the competing sales match the Prime Day price exactly. This is a good way to save even if you object to shopping on Amazon.

Is Prime Day Worth It?

It depends. For some items, Prime-exclusive event prices tend to be among the lowest we see all year. That's especially true for Amazon hardware, like Kindles, Fire tablets, Fire TV sticks, and Echo devices. The kicker is that prices on nearly everything fluctuate throughout the year, and some products are discounted on a frequent basis. Even if the price is good, a deal on a product that goes on sale all the time diminishes the overall quality of that offer.

The sheer volume of deals promoted by Amazon during sales like Prime Day is a blessing and a curse. The truly standout discounts can be difficult to pinpoint—there's so much stuff on sale that just browsing the site can feel overwhelming. But if you're in the market for something specific, there's a good chance the item you want will be discounted. We've seen some fantastic Prime-exclusive discounts in the past, ranging from dirt-cheap Kindles and video doorbells to elusive price drops on gaming consoles and office furniture. The tricky part is finding the diamonds in the rough.

WIRED covers legitimately good deals all year long, including during Prime Day. Our policy is to only cover deals on products someone from our team has personally used and would buy or has bought themselves, to avoid promoting cheap junk. Maybe it'll be a product we've reviewed or an item we use in our day-to-day lives. We also only cover actual deals—if the price isn't lower than it normally is, we don't include it. We aim to provide pricing context as well. Our tips below will help you find those great discounts on your own—in the same ways that we would. No gatekeeping here.

How Do I Know Whether a Deal Is Good?

ABC: Always be checking (prices, that is). Researching an item's price is the most important aspect of determining the quality of a discount. Don't fall prey to deceptive marketing language and inflated MSRP prices. The easiest step is to take a second to Google the items you're considering so you can see the price across multiple stores. Amazon product pages now feature a Price History link to see up to 365 days of pricing history, though it may not always be accurate.

One tool we use is CamelCamelCamel, which tracks Amazon's prices over time. Paste the Amazon link or ASIN (found in the Product Information section on the Amazon product page) into CamelCamelCamel's search bar to see the item's lowest recorded price and its average price, and how frequently the price fluctuates. Some deals, such as Lightning Deals, are excluded from the pricing history, but this works for most items. It's useful to see what an item has sold for in the past. And while Amazon's Alexa for Shopping chatbot has price history information, it isn't always reliable and often misses context (as evidenced by our personal testing). We also like Keepa, which has an extension (available for multiple browsers) that shows the recent price history for products directly on the Amazon page so you don't have to open a new tab. When in doubt, check multiple sources.

Tech.title: MacOS 27 Golden Gate: Top New Features
Tech.content:
Apple's latest version of its Mac operating system officially rolled out on September 14. MacOS 27 Golden Gate was announced at WWDC in June, but it's now available to download right on your Mac—assuming you have a compatible one.

The launch of Siri AI is the huge new feature, which is Apple's first serious attempt to integrate AI capabilities deeply into macOS. I've been playing around with the software update for months, and now it's available for anyone to try out.

Updated September 2026: We've added some hands-on impressions now that macOS 27 is officially out in the world.

Is Your Mac Compatible With macOS Golden Gate? AccordionItemContainerButton LargeChevron The new update, macOS 27 Golden Gate, is only compatible with Apple Silicon Macs. Last year, Apple announced that macOS 26 Tahoe would be the last update to support Intel-powered Macs. Here's the full list of supported devices: MacBook Neo (2026)

MacBook Pro (2020 and later)

MacBook Air (2020 and later)

Mac mini (2020 and later)

iMac (2021 and later)

Mac Studio (2022 and later)

Mac Pro (2023 and later) Some of the more advanced Apple Intelligence features, such as the improved Voice Mode, are exclusive to newer Macs. Those more advanced modes require an M3 Mac or newer with at least 12 GB of RAM. That rules out the MacBook Neo and lots of MacBook Airs from before 2024. One more caveat: Siri AI is currently English-only and will not be immediately available in the EU or China due to regulatory concerns. How to Install macOS 27 Golden Gate AccordionItemContainerButton LargeChevron The MacOS Golden Gate beta has been available since July, but the official release is now available to download and safe to install on your Mac if you want to try out the new features. Like always, just head over to System Settings > General > Software Update. From there, you should see macOS Golden Gate 27 available, with the option to Update Now or Update Tonight.

Meet the New Siri

Siri AI on iPadOS. Courtesy of Apple

Siri on Mac never made a lot of sense, and I can't imagine it has ever been used much. But this new version of the chatbot, known as Siri AI, looks a bit more tailored for this new version of macOS Golden Gate. It carries over a lot of the new features that the iOS and iPadOS versions have, including a dedicated app, screen awareness, automatic proofreading, personal context, and the improved, customizable voice experience. Most importantly, the new Apple Foundation Models that Siri runs on are based on Google Gemini, giving it highly improved natural language processing as well as the latest computer vision and image-generation models.

I could see a lot of Mac users, especially those who are weary (or afraid) of going to ChatGPT.com, getting their first real exposure to modern AI chatbots through Siri AI. Unfortunately, it’s currently still in Beta. It’s turned off by default, and in Settings, it states that Siri AI is “being rolled out gradually.” That's a shame considering how long we've been waiting for it, but Apple clearly wants to release this to the wider public as carefully as possible. Reports online indicate that some people were clearing the wait list early on within minutes. I was not that lucky, however, and have been waiting for almost an entire day at the time of writing. Apple hasn't indicated how extensive the wait list is or how long it will take to come out of beta.

Once you do have access, though, Siri should now be systemwide. It can be pulled up from anywhere on the desktop, where it’s accessible from a simple right click in the context window. One example of how this might work is with documents. In Finder, you can select a few files and then right click, then click on Siri AI to start prompting right in the Siri AI app. It's also being built into Spotlight. Right now, Spotlight is primarily just for finding things on your computer. But now Apple says that if you ask it a question that's more suited for Siri, it'll automatically answer using Siri AI and open a chat window so you can continue the Siri conversation. Siri also has Visual Intelligence on the Mac. If you take a screenshot, Siri can be immediately pulled up and prompted to answer questions about or take action on what’s in that image.

For more information on how Siri AI works across other platforms, check out our full breakdown of everything you can do with the new app.

Apple Intelligence Apps

Photograph: Luke Larsen

The broader rollout of this new version of Siri is also happening across a variety of first-party Apple apps. Safari is getting the biggest update. It's had tab groups since 2021, but browser tabs have always had to be organized and managed manually. Now, there's something called Topics in Safari, which feels like a smarter way to organize tabs. Using AI, Safari will automatically combine tabs together into topics, which can then be closed out or saved for later as a tab group.

Tech.title: I Trained a Fly’s Brain to Generate WIRED Story Ideas
Tech.content:
Meet PitchFly, WIRED’s latest editorial recruit.

He has 165,112 neurons, and they’re all trained to generate story ideas. A sampling of his early output: “The Hidden Weather Problem Inside Surveillance”; “The Engineers Who Think Elon Musk Needs Less Computer Security”; and my personal favorite, “Everyone Wants Cooking. Nobody Has Solved Donald Trump.”

PitchFly uses a detailed map of the brain of a male drosophila—the common fruit fly. Developed by researchers from Google and a number of academic institutions, the map, known as a connectome, captures the way that 166,000 neurons and 125 million connecting synapses fire in response to stimuli. In essence, you can use it to simulate how a fly would respond to lots of stuff—it’s a very simple version of artificial intelligence based on charting real biological intelligence.

Because the researchers open-sourced it, you can easily use AI to import the connectome into a project with a little prompting. For PitchFly, I vibe coded a project in which the tiny digital drosophila brain generates story ideas. (I’m not sure why the fly has a little hat on, but I like its style.) This involved scraping together hundreds of the most popular story headlines from the site from the past year and feeding them into the connectome. I had Codex do the hard work, and it decided that the most efficient approach was to turn the headlines into words and phrases, then transform them into a representation that a neural network could understand. The connectome was fed the best-performing stories and told to generate its own ideas based on that.

In other words, this isn’t a fly-based language model—although someone apparently created one of those. The fly brain has no idea what any of the words mean, or if any of it makes sense. It’s just remixing the patterns it has seen in pleasing new ways. A cynic might suggest this is exactly how some journalists generate their own pitches, but I think that’s a bit unfair—and judging by its lunatic ideas, PitchFly won’t be replacing me anytime soon:

The Tiny Shift in Agentic AI Is Rewriting the Rules of Food and Drink

What Security News Is Quietly Doing to Donald Trump

The Race to Reinvent Privacy Before Artificial Intelligence Breaks

Is China About to Make Digital Syndication Obsolete?

In the future, perhaps I could have the program continue to learn by reading new WIRED headlines. For now, though, this seems like a decent proof of concept, not to mention evidence at last that the average WIRED writer is intellectually superior to a fruit fly.

After the connectome’s release in early September, dozens of other weird and wonderful projects powered by fruit-fly intelligence sprang up.

An X user called Lyra Bubbles, for instance, demo’d a project that involved training the virtual fly brain to play the VR game Beat Saber. Alex Wormuth, a software engineer at Coinbase, created StonkFly, which uses the fly’s tiny brain to decide how to trade stocks. (It’s losing money, but it’s doing surprisingly well, all things considered.)

“The fly brings lighthearted, humorous relief” at a time when everyone is worried about the existential risks of AI, Wormuth told me in a DM. He says he found playing with the fruit fly connectome philosophically fascinating, too. “It sparks questions about ethics of this and whether there is any consciousness [in the replication of fly’s brain],” he says.

Tech.title: The Best Movies to Stream This Month (September 2026)
Tech.content:
Fall is here, and the autumnal turn marks a season of returns. Back to school, back to work—and when it comes to the best films on streaming services, back to some of the best films of yesteryear.

September finds John Carpenter’s brilliant 1982 remake of The Thing crawling its way onto Prime Video, Luc Besson’s mind-bending and eye-popping The Fifth Element on Netflix, and an unexpected blast from the past coming to Hulu in the form of The X-Files: I Want to Believe—Vrach Frankenshteyn, an R-rated director’s cut of 2008’s second cinematic case for Mulder and Scully, now closer to creator Chris Carter’s original vision.

Even the new arrivals have a vintage flair this month though. Star Wars spinoff The Mandalorian and Grogu brings the big-screen bounty hunters back to Disney+ for a retro-tinged adventure, Netflix’s Mobile Suit Gundam: Hathaway expands on the world of the classic 1970s anime series, and Edge of Tomorrow on Paramount+ shows the past can be hard to escape at the best of times.

Here are WIRED’s picks of the best movies to watch right now.

The Mandalorian & Grogu

Sure, The Mandalorian and Grogu has the dubious distinction of being the lowest-grossing live-action Star Wars movie ever (only 2008’s animated Clone Wars performed worse). And yes, for fans of the Disney+ space western series, a full fourth season might have been more welcome (and the three seasons of homework beforehand may have put off wider audiences anyway). Yet this spinoff is, in its own way, the “purest” Star Wars movie in years, capturing the feel of the classic serials that originally inspired George Lucas all those decades ago.

Tech.title: AI’s Rising Costs Cast Doubts on Cloud Gaming’s Future
Tech.content:
Despite never gaining the same traction as major gaming consoles or premium gaming PCs, cloud gaming services have steadily persisted since their rise in the 2010s. Cloud gaming services let people play video games by streaming them live over the internet. The pitch is that you don’t have to buy expensive PC gear or invest in a game console plus the price of individual titles to play AAA (or lots of not-quite-AAA) games; you just need to stream them with a subscription.

Sure, Google’s ambitious Stadia gaming service shut down in 2023, but similar services that offer streaming video game play over an internet connection from Nvidia, Microsoft’s Xbox, Sony’s PlayStation and Amazon’s Prime have kept the dream alive.

But cloud gaming services have struggled to go mainstream due to the inherent challenge of delivering consistent gameplay in an inconsistent world of laggy internet connections and millions of hardware options. (A recent New York Times headline: The Best Cloud Gaming Services Aren’t Great (Yet).) And now they may be facing an even bigger challenge: the cost of providing their services is skyrocketing, as demand for AI compute power and other data needs is making the services that data centers provide much more expensive.

As Chris Plante, co-founder of Polygon and writer and podcaster at Post Games, describes it, cloud gaming has been a “white whale” for gaming companies for the last decade. However, demand has fallen short of expectations, and costs are now rising.

“Companies sold audiences on the idea of cheaper compute that could be leased from a data center, only for data center compute to become more expensive than ever, leaving those companies with a sales pitch that no longer adds up,” Plante said.

The idea that the math behind cloud gaming no longer makes sense is starting to ring alarm bells in gaming communities. A recent Guardian story asked simply, “What happened?” to the promise of cloud gaming, and pointed to limits imposed on services like Nvidia’s GeForce Now and Xbox Cloud Gaming this year as an indicator that we may see some options disappear. A BigGo Finance analysis published this week said cloud gaming is being squeezed by big tech’s AI infrastructure needs, with some of that demand driven by the same companies that offer these cloud gaming subscriptions.

What’s changed this year in cloud gaming?

At the start of the year, all users of Nvidia’s GeForce Now, including those who’d been grandfathered in for the prior year, were subject to playtime limits on their accounts: 100 hours, with the option to roll over 15 hours of unused time per month.

That meant players who were already paying $10 to $20 a month for one of the game streaming plans would need to pay an additional $3 to $6 for an extra 15-hour block of time, depending on their tier.

Also this year, Microsoft’s overhaul of its Game Pass program, which has included price reductions, placed similar limits on Xbox Cloud Gaming usage that will go into effect in November. When that happens, Game Pass Ultimate subscribers will be capped at 15 hours of cloud gaming per month, while Premium and Essential subscribers will get 10 and 5 hours, respectively. All tiers will have the option to pay extra for more cloud gaming, but Microsoft has not revealed what overages will cost. The company said at the time, “Moving to monthly limits allows us to keep offering the service while continuing to invest in its reliability and performance. We understand that for some players the practical result is a higher cost.”

When the change was announced, Microsoft tipped its hand about how unpopular the service is, revealing that only 4% of Xbox users would be affected.

Rumors swirled earlier this year that Xbox Game Pass would be able to select an ad-supported tier offering discounted subscriptions, similar to what Netflix and Amazon Prime Video offer, but that hasn’t materialized yet. Microsoft confirmed over the summer that it’s testing out an ad tier.

Microsoft declined to respond to questions about more recent reports suggesting it might separate Cloud Gaming from Game Pass entirely and make it an add-on for an additional fee. “We will share more details about the cloud updates that we announced earlier this month closer to November’s launch,” a spokesperson said in an email.

Amazon pushes back on the cloudy outlook for game streaming

Courtroom Chaos Starring Snoop Dogg is an exclusive for Amazon’s Luna cloud gaming service. Amazon Game Studios

Over the last few years, perhaps because of the attention Amazon’s other business segments receive, the company’s Luna game streaming has not drawn a lot of attention. But the retail giant has been making a lot of changes since last year, rolling its Prime Gaming service into Luna and premiering original games like Courtroom Chaos with Snoop Dogg, as well as popular third-party titles like Hogwarts Legacy and Indiana Jones and the Great Circle.

In its most recent update, Luna added Star Wars: Outlaws and Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora for streaming at no added cost to anyone with an Amazon Prime account. It’s also been introducing multiplayer games that can be played through its Prime Video app, similar to the way Netflix offers video games (or links to app downloads) in its video streaming apps.

The head of these efforts, games industry veteran and head of Amazon Gaming Jeff Gattis, told CNET that Amazon’s AWS service allows it to operate Luna “efficiently at enormous scale, and that scale is exactly what makes a service like Luna viable.”

Gattis said that what’s missing in the doomsaying about cloud gaming is the recognition that there’s a large segment of gamers, perhaps casual ones, who can’t keep up with the rising costs of gaming hardware.

“We actually see this as cloud gaming’s moment,” Gattis said. “The cost of entry for players keeps climbing with console hardware prices rising, high-end PCs costing more than ever, and games themselves getting more expensive. For a lot of people, that’s becoming a real barrier.”

At least for Amazon, he said, cloud gaming is not going away anytime soon.

“Amazon has a long track record of building services for the long term, and Luna, powered by AWS and integrated into Prime, is built to last as an accessible and affordable way to play,” he said.

Tech.title: Meta Reportedly Creating Glasses Without Cameras After ‘Pervert’ Uproar
Tech.content:
The backlash has spoken. Meta reportedly is developing smart glasses without cameras amid a general anxiety about the wearable technology’s potential for privacy violations and following incidents of people using what have been dubbed “pervert glasses” to record videos of women without their permission or knowledge.

According to reporting from The Information, Meta wants to begin selling the new glasses — called Luna — in October and could introduce the new devices at its Connect developer conference next week. Meta Connect is scheduled for Sept. 23-24 and will be livestreamed.

The Information said Luna will have two styles, Clubmaster and Burbank. The smart glasses will have six microphones, along with speakers directed at the user’s ears. Wearers can speak to and listen to the Meta AI chatbot by pressing a button on the side of the glasses, The Information reported.

A representative for Meta didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.



Meta’s Ray-Ban smart glasses have gained an unfortunate reputation. News reports have cited men using the device’s cameras to record women — for instance asking to go out on a date while secretly recording the encounter — and then posting the videos on social media. The smart glasses have also been used to film pranks and harassment interactions.

One woman told CNN she had a conversation with a man at an airport and later discovered that he had posted several videos on social media of interactions he had with other women. Despite being asked by the woman at the airport not to post their conversation online, he did it anyway.



Although there is a small LED light that turns on and blinks during recording, some people have removed the light or found ways to camouflage the LED so that people would not know they were being recorded. Meta rolled out a software update in late July that would deactivate the camera if the LED light was tampered with in any way.

But as CNET’s Scott Stein writes, it is difficult to spot the white LED light in bright daylight, and the Meta glasses look almost identical to the non-smart Ray-Ban glasses that have been around for decades. Stein also reported in June that Meta CTO Andrew Bosworth had indicated the company’s interest in releasing a less-expensive, camera-free version of its smart glasses that would focus on audio capabilities.

Austin Evans, a YouTube tech reviewer with nearly 6 million subscribers, said he rarely wears the Meta Ray-Bans anymore because of the bad vibes associated with them. He said he’s talked with folks at Meta about why glasses without cameras would be a good idea.

“It’s pretty simple technically, I would assume,” Evans told CNET. “It probably would allow them to slim the glasses down a bit. But most importantly it will be a really strong step toward removing the stigma around wearing them.”

Tech.title: Cox Customers Officially Make the Jump to Spectrum
Tech.content:
Two of the country’s largest internet providers have officially become one, as existing Cox customers will start getting their monthly internet bills from Spectrum from Wednesday.

Charter, which sells phone, internet and TV services under the Spectrum brand, agreed to buy Cox in May 2025, but the deal didn’t clear its final hurdle until the California Public Utilities Commission approved it last month.

The acquisition creates the largest internet provider in the country, with Charter now boasting more than 35 million customers. While internet monopolies are a major problem in the US — over a third of Americans only have access to one or no internet provider — this acquisition won’t necessarily make that problem worse. That’s because Charter and Cox have very little overlap in the areas where they operate.

“No consumer is going to lose a competitive offering they currently have,” Blair Levin, a telecom industry analyst at New Street Research, told CNET. “There’s no reduction of competition in any relevant geographical product market.”

The deal could be a welcome change for Cox customers. Cox received a score of 68/100 in the most recent American Customer Satisfaction Index survey, while Spectrum earned a 71/100.

However, a CNET analysis of internet plans found Spectrum’s price hikes to be steeper, with Spectrum increasing prices by an average of $37 monthly after one or two years, depending on the location. Cox’s plans increased by $28 per month, but only after two years.

Spectrum says Cox customers won’t have to do a thing: Prices and plans will stay the same, and they can keep using their existing Cox equipment. Spectrum is also offering a year of free mobile service to Cox customers who make the jump to Spectrum Mobile, plus a slew of new streaming subscriptions for customers on eligible Cox Contour TV plans.

Some critics argued that the Federal Communications Commission should have done more to help consumers before granting Charter approval.

“The FCC approved the largest cable merger in nearly a decade and did not require Charter to do anything it wasn’t already planning to do,” John Bergmayer, legal director at the consumer advocacy group Public Knowledge, said in a statement. “Consumers, as always, will bear the costs of reduced competition.”

As part of the approval process, Charter agreed to move all of Cox’s offshore jobs to America within 18 months. According to a post on its website, Charter says it has a 100% US-based workforce as of Dec. 31, 2025.

Tech.title: Gears of War: E-Day and Minecraft Dungeons 2 Headline Xbox Game Pass September 2026 Additions
Tech.content:
Microsoft continues to modify its Xbox Game Pass service as the company tries to get a handle on how expensive it is. The company said that in November it will eliminate the unlimited cloud gaming perk that comes with a subscription and instead limit the number of hours based on the membership level. Rumors circulated on Monday claiming other changes were coming to the service, including the removal of Day 1 games, an ad-supported tier and a decrease in subscription costs. Microsoft didn’t confirm or deny the rumors, only saying it didn’t “have any changes to announce today or plans that have been finalized.”

September’s Xbox Game Pass lineup has some heavy hitters coming in at the end of the month and at the start of October. Gears of War: E-Day, a prequel to the series, is the biggest title coming to the Xbox platform before Grand Theft Auto 6‘s release on Nov. 19. Microsoft, like every other game publisher, hopes to get its big guns out before the gaming world is completely taken over by the next GTA game.

Xbox Game Pass, a CNET Editors’ Choice award pick, offers a wide selection of games you can play on your Xbox Series X, Xbox Series S, Xbox One and PC or mobile device for as little as $10 per month. With a subscription to the higher-tiered Game Pass Ultimate ($23 per month), you can access hundreds of games, including new ones the day they’re released, each month.

Here are all the games Xbox is bringing to Game Pass in September.

RuneScape: Dragonwilds

Game Pass Ultimate, Premium and PC Game Pass subscribers can play on Sept. 15.

Dragons have returned to the forgotten land of Ashenfall, leaving players to survive in a dangerous new wilderness. Gather resources, craft equipment, build a home and develop your skills as you explore the continent and uncover the secrets behind the Dragon Queen.

Kernel Hearts

Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass subscribers can play on Sept. 17.

This anime-style action RPG combines fast-paced combat with roguelike progression and optional co-op. Choose from four characters with distinct abilities and playstyles as you climb the Tower of Babel, developing your skills and learning more about your companions along the way.

Dune: Awakening

Game Pass Ultimate, Premium and PC Game Pass subscribers can play on Sept. 22.

Set on the harsh desert world of Arrakis, Dune: Awakening blends survival mechanics with open-world exploration and RPG elements. Gather resources, build your base, craft equipment and uncover a cinematic story as you attempt to survive on one of the most unforgiving planets in the universe.

Well Dweller

Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass subscribers can play on Sept. 22.

This dark fairy tale adventure puts you in control of Glimmer, a tiny bird armed with nothing more than a matchstick. Explore a troubled kingdom, meet its unusual inhabitants, battle dangerous creatures and navigate a sprawling Metroidvania world as you try to save Glimmer’s family from a wicked queen.

Mad King Redemption

Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass subscribers can play on Sept. 23.

This 2.5D beat ’em up combines classic arcade-style fighting with roguelite progression, meaning each run offers something different. Fight through waves of corrupted enemies, build up your character and attempt to break the Mad King free from his growing insanity.

Minecraft Dungeons 2

Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass subscribers can play on Sept. 29.

This sequel sends players beyond the familiar Minecraft world and into the mysterious Sift. Team up with friends to battle new enemies, explore unfamiliar environments and collect gear that can be customized to suit your play style as you prepare for increasingly difficult challenges.

Gears of War: E-Day

Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass subscribers can play on Oct. 6.

Set 14 years before the original Gears of War, this prequel follows Marcus Fenix and Dominic Santiago as the Locust Horde launches its devastating first attack. The campaign explores the beginning of the conflict that would define the series, putting you in the middle of humanity’s fight for survival.

Other games coming to Xbox Game Pass

Those are some of the games Microsoft is bringing to Xbox Game Pass soon, but the company is adding more this month. Here are the other games you can try soon.

Marvel Cosmic Invasion: Coming to Game Pass Premium on Sept. 16. Previously on Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass.

Planet of Lana 2: Coming to Game Pass Premium on Sept. 16. Previously on Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass.

Routine: Coming to Game Pass Premium on Sept. 16. Previously on Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass.

Ultimate Sheep Raccoon: Coming to Game Pass Premium on Sept. 16. Previously on Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass.

Call of Duty: Black Ops 6: Coming to Game Pass Premium on Sept. 25. Previously on Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass.

Keeper: Coming to Game Pass Premium on Oct. 2. Previously on Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass.

Games leaving Game Pass soon

While Microsoft is adding those games to different Game Pass tiers, the company is removing eight others on Sept. 30. You still have time to play these games for the first time, or finish your campaign, before you have to buy them separately, but you should hurry.

For more on Xbox, learn what other titles you can play, plus read our Xbox Game Pass review and discover which Game Pass plan is right for you.

Tech.title: Apple’s Health App Hits Developer Beta. I Got the Inside Scoop From Apple’s VP of Health and Fitness
Tech.content:
Last week at Apple’s “Surprise and Shine” event, Dr. Sumbul Desai, Apple’s VP of Health and Fitness, announced the redesigned Health app and its fresh features. Between the new Insights tab with Apple Intelligence-powered suggestions, a Longevity tab that shows your Health Age, a readiness score, movement assessments, a blood panel and curated doctor videos, my head was swimming with questions. The following day, I sat down for a video chat with Desai for deeper insight into Apple’s reimagined health platform.

Now, on Wednesday, the new Health app debuted in the first developer beta of iOS 27.2. Some announced features will be available in later betas, including personalized summaries under the Insights tab, personalized recommendations and the ability to order a blood panel from Quest Diagnostics.

“Features will roll out progressively,” Apple said in an email. “Feedback during the beta period will help us continue refining it ahead of the public release in late 2026.”

Here’s everything you can expect to uncover in the Health app and the features you shouldn’t sleep on.

From data spreadsheet to intelligent experience

Launched in 2014, the Health app was initially intended to be like a spreadsheet, with data flowing in, Desai explained. However, the team realized they wanted more from the app, so it evolved over the past 12 years into what Desai now calls “an experience.”

Those at the helm of the Health app’s 2026 makeover considered how to leverage Apple’s machine learning and AI to help people live healthier, while also personalizing the app’s recommendations and turning it into an intelligent hub, not unlike the iPhone itself. For instance, as you open the app and move through your day, different screens appear to reflect your health status.

Movement assessments have also been added to provide an even more complete picture of a user’s health and track progress or decline. Desai described them as a “mini physical” you can complete at home.

All assessments under the app’s Longevity tab are science-based and contribute to a rainbow-petal visual that illuminates your state of health. Some assessments rely on vision-based AI models that integrate the phone’s camera, marking the first time Apple has used the camera for health.

The current iteration of the Health app is just the beginning and was designed to set in motion the next era of the team’s work in health and fitness, as Desai said those working on the app still feel they have more to do.

The Longevity tab’s rainbow visual. Apple

Health Age: Biological vs. birthday

One standout feature from Apple’s event was the Health app’s Longevity tab, which will include a feature called Health Age that uses health metrics such as your VO2 max (the maximum amount of oxygen your body consumes during exercise), resting heart rate, sleep and heart rate variability, along with lab data such as LDL cholesterol and A1c for your average blood sugar level, to provide your biological age, which represents how your body is aging on a cellular level when compared to your actual age.

Apple’s own Heart and Movement Study, which it applies across all its health products, informs both Health Age and Readiness, which uses your activity data, daytime and overnight vitals and sleep data to tell you about your capacity for the day ahead.

The five-year Heart and Movement Study was conducted in collaboration with the American Heart Association and Brigham and Women’s Hospital to explore the connection between heart health and physical activity. Apple used that data to create the normative ranges for the insights it provides in the app.

While Desai acknowledged the Health Age assessment is more of a “fun way to look at your health habits” and that no one can tell you your actual biological age, it’s another way to provide insight and suggest healthy habits users can integrate into their lives.

I’m also hoping my Health Age is lower than my actual age. Apple

Apple’s secret sauce

Apple isn’t the first company to offer features such as a readiness score or biological age, but Desai said that it stands out from competitors because of its unique perspectives, experiences and the science behind its work.

“When we first started our work in health, when we announced our irregular heart rhythm notifications and ECG, those were clinically validated scientific features,” she said. Desai likened those early days to building a muscle that lets the team create impactful products the medical community will appreciate, and users can easily understand.

That muscle Apple first built has been exercised with all the Health app’s new features, as Desai said that everything is rooted in science. On her team, for instance, physical therapists graded each movement in the app’s mobility assessments to ensure that when a movement is picked up and a result is given, it’s graded the way an actual physical therapist would grade it.

Uniting science and expertise, Desai said that’s what Apple brings to the table, and its Health app experience.

The new Health app’s ‘sleeper hit’

Much of the discourse following Apple’s event has been about the new readiness score and Health Age. I was curious what Desai felt was the “sleeper hit” feature that didn’t get as much attention.

“It’s actually the assessments,” Desai said. “You’re going to be able to, on a regular basis, do a push-up test and a core test and see if you’re improving. Then we give you insights and things that you can do to improve, and then you can test again. It’s almost like having a physical therapist or a trainer.”

The VO2 max test, in particular, marks the first time Apple’s doing an on-demand, in-the-moment VO2 max test.

You can then take all your assessment results, and the Health app will put them into a report you can share with your doctor.

A person performing a movement assessment using their iPhone. Apple/Screenshot by CNET

Homing in on your body’s big players

Based on its new assessments, the Longevity tab’s visualization has seven tabs: heart health, sleep, mental wellbeing, movement health, metabolic health, hearing and nutrition. But how did Apple narrow it down to those seven?

“We picked areas where we felt like we had the appropriate data to comment on,” Desai explained. “For example, we do a cardiovascular risk score through some of the questions. It’s based on traditional risk scores and cardiovascular risk scores that are done.”

The team prioritized information they believe people will use and assessments they’ll complete, while ensuring the chosen health areas feel holistic and will help people concerned about long-term quality of life.

“There’s still more that we think we can do, but this is where we’re starting,” Desai stated. In other words, Longevity’s rainbow visual could gain more colors in the future.

Keeping privacy at Apple’s core

When it comes to its Health app, Desai said privacy is where they start and end.

“Candidly, we may not always be the first to market, but when we release something, we can stand behind it from a privacy standpoint,” Desai stated. “All the features you saw [announced] are no different. … It’s part of the conversation every day, and up till the day that the products are launched.”

Apple will hold off on releasing a product if it hasn’t met its privacy bar. The team behind the Health app also uses a checks-and-balances system, having other teams review their work to ensure they are nailing their privacy approach.

“In this world where more things happen in the cloud, we want to make sure that’s all encrypted and private, which is why we have Private Cloud Compute,” said Desai. Private Cloud Compute is Apple’s cloud intelligence system designed for private AI processing.

The team’s approach is end-to-end because privacy matters for all your data, not just health data.

Apple Intelligence has suggestions

The Health app’s new Insights tab uses Apple Intelligence to analyze your health metrics and provide a timely summary that updates throughout the day.

“We also make suggestions,” said Desai. “For example, if you have an injury or you’re trying to work on your mobility, we’ll give you suggestions on the types of exercises you might be doing.”

It’s another example of how the app is evolving from a database to something that more closely resembles a personalized health advisor.

The daily insights are meant to be bite-size pieces of information that are one small thing you can do for your health each day. Some days these insights may be interesting; other days, you might be given information you already know.

Under Insights, the For You section will use your data to offer personalized recommendations and relevant articles. Apple

Health on a cellular level, explained

For $119, the new Health app will let you purchase a blood panel with over 50 biomarkers through Quest Diagnostics. You can also get your blood pressure, height, weight and waist and hip circumferences measured. All this helps provide a more complete picture of metabolic health.

The revamped app will include videos from doctors that help people better understand what they see in the app.

“When you get your assessment results, you’ll actually see your own data in the videos where they’re explained by clinicians,” said Desai. “We have a physician, a physical therapist, a sleep expert, a mental health expert. The reason we did that is, for certain things, gamification works, but for certain things, you just want to know the information in an easy-to-understand way from an authoritative resource.”

While an expert explains the subject at hand, your health data, whether from your labs or your Apple Watch, will be overlaid on the video so you can see it as you learn more.

Ultimately, Desai doesn’t see the future of the Health app as one size fits all. Depending on the feature, the team always chooses what makes health as accessible and understandable as possible. In a world with an abundance of health data, perhaps that’s what matters most: ensuring people understand the numbers they see on their devices, and knowing what to do with them once the screen goes black.

Tech.title: Nintendo Urges Switch Owners to Update Their Firmware After Security Exploit Discovered
Tech.content:
Owners of the original Nintendo Switch should patch a security exploit immediately, especially if they use the game console in public. Nintendo announced the vulnerability on Sept. 10, shortly after the company released its latest 23.0.0 firmware update.

The vulnerability applies only to original Nintendo Switch owners who use the Send to Smartphone feature. This feature generates a QR code on the Switch that users can scan with a smartphone, letting them transfer game captures and screenshots directly to a phone.

The exploit also affects people playing Super Mario Kart: Home Circuit on the physical cartridge, as the game uses a QR code to establish a wireless link with nearby players.

Should someone else scan the QR code before you, they can connect their device to your Switch and use the connection to run unauthorized code on your Switch or steal information stored on the game console. Since your account information is stored on your Switch, that’s information you don’t want in the hands of someone else.

A Nintendo representative did not immediately respond to a request for further comment.

The exploit does not affect the Nintendo Switch 2.

How to fix the problem

The fix is simple. Nintendo released update 23.0.0 on Sept. 9, which fixes the exploit. It’s recorded as CVE-2026-82079, which is “a stock-based buffer overflow vulnerability” that lets attackers within wireless range execute code. It only affects the original Switch on firmware versions older than 23.0.0.

To update your Nintendo Switch, head to System Settings > System > System Update to apply the update. Follow any additional on-screen prompts to install the update.

Nintendo says that those who can’t immediately update their firmware can avoid the issue by only using the Send to Smartphone feature at home, where attackers can’t see them, or by not playing Super Mario Kart: Home Circuit in public. The gaming giant also recommends not scanning any QR codes with any device that isn’t yours.

People who only play games at home are protected from this exploit and don’t have to worry about it.

Tech.title: Anthropic Simplifies Claude’s Cowork and Design Tools
Tech.content:
Anthropic is breaking down some of the silos inside its AI chatbot, Claude. Starting now, Claude Cowork and Claude Design will just be inside your normal Claude experience, Anthropic announced on Wednesday.

Anthropic has quickly made its AI a new kind of staple in the modern workplace, competing with OG tech heavyweights like Google and Microsoft. But AI adoption in the workplace has been rocky, from unclear policies to haphazard implementation and “work slop” that is making some people’s days longer and more unpleasant. Changes like these aren’t big, but they’re one step Anthropic is taking to make its AI more usable and, ideally, make the people who use it more productive and inclined to return to the chatbot.

The idea behind the redesigned interface is to make it easier to access the Claude services you need right where you start your AI work — the prompt bar. So you won’t need to bounce between the dedicated Claude Cowork experience for writing your reports and the beta Claude Design tab to turn that report into a slide deck, for example. You can still use custom project folders to keep all your related chats and project files in one place.

Notice how you can select Docs, Slides and Design directly from your prompting window. Anthropic

Excluded from this redesign is Claude Code. This makes sense because coding is a different kind of AI activity, where a separate interface is necessary.

You can also create documents and slide decks more easily through new, dedicated “output” widgets called, you guessed it, Claude Docs and Slides. You can share these AI-generated files with other people to edit using a shareable link or download as a PDF or PowerPoint. Similar to the Design beta, employees using Claude through an enterprise plan may not have access to the new tools, depending on their workplace’s AI permissions.

These changes will first roll out to people on the most expensive Pro and Max plans over the next few weeks, on web, mobile and desktop. Anthropic plans to bring it to free and Team users afterward. Folks on enterprise plans won’t see changes immediately either.

Tech.title: Seeing ‘Optimizing Search and Siri’ After the iOS 27 Update? Here’s What’s Actually Happening
Tech.content:
If you’ve updated to iOS 27 and spotted an “Optimizing Search and Siri” message in Settings, there’s no need to stop using your iPhone or assume something has gone wrong. The message means iOS is rebuilding its search index, a process that becomes necessary after a major update because a major iOS update often implements a brand-new search infrastructure, and the system cannot simply update your existing index. It must crawl through your entire storage drive from scratch. Here’s what that means for your phone’s performance while it’s happening and how to help it finish faster.

You can download iOS 27 now by going to Settings > General > Software Update > Update Now and following the prompts on your screen.

At June’s Worldwide Developers Conference, Apple announced that it was rebuilding its Search interface for iOS 27. The company said the restructure would make searching across your device faster, more reliable and more accurate. In order to do that, iOS 27 has to reindex items across your iPhone. So after you update, you’ll see a banner in Settings that reads “Optimizing Search and Siri.” This is a normal part of the update, and it could take a while to finish, but the good news is you can still use your iPhone during this process.

Here’s what you need to know about the indexing and optimization process once you download iOS 27.

What is indexing?

Data indexing is the process of scanning and organizing metadata from data assets into an index so it can be easily searched.



“Think of it like the index of a book,” data management company Komprise wrote online. “[The index] doesn’t hold the content, but it tells you where to find it, and what’s inside.”

Apple’s support page about Spotlight indexing says that Spotlight search indexes your iPhone when you first set up your device, as data changes on your device and after you update your iPhone. So your device has reindexed before and you likely never noticed – I know I didn’t.

Apple also notes that your iPhone’s index “stays on your device and isn’t shared with Apple or your other devices.”

Indexing can take hours or days

You can still use your iPhone, even when it’s indexing. LuckyDuck via Getty Images

Apple’s support page notes that indexing could take anywhere from a couple hours to a few days. When I updated my iPhone to a beta version of iOS 27, my iPhone took a couple hours to index, but the more stuff you have stored on your phone, the longer it will take.

The process takes longer this time around because Apple rebuilt its Search interface in iOS 27. So the update isn’t just adding a few more things to the index, it’s implementing a new search system.

That means the system isn’t just crawling through the new stuff — it needs to go back through all the data in your phone. Think of it like cataloging new items you’ve bought versus creating an inventory of everything in your home.

Apple does offer a few suggestions on how to speed up the process:

Plug your device into a power source.

Connect your device to Wi-Fi.

Don’t use your iPhone.

OK, can I still use my iPhone?

You can! Indexing doesn’t prevent you from using your iPhone, but it goes faster if you set the phone aside.

If you do use your iPhone during the process, your Spotlight search results might be incomplete because it hasn’t finished indexing. Otherwise, your device should operate as usual. Which is good because I couldn’t imagine going without my phone for a few days at this point – don’t judge me.

Spotlight search still not working?

If your iPhone is finished indexing – the banner in Settings will go away – and you’re still running into issues, you should review your Search settings and make sure Spotlight has access to your apps. Here’s how to check.

Tap Settings. Tap Search.

From here, you can adjust what shows up in Spotlight, and near the bottom of the menu, you can review which apps Spotlight has access to. You can tap into each app to grant or revoke Spotlight permission.

However, there doesn’t seem to be a way to grant or revoke Spotlight access across all apps at once, so you have to go into each individual app to do this.

For more on Apple, here’s what to know about the iPhone Duo and everything Apple announced at its “Surprise and shine” event.
